- <a id="ev-II-0013"></a>**16 am Màrt, FE 59** — *The Hall declines the stream* (Allt an Àigh). Muireach Liath rules that Allt an Àigh belongs to the ancestors and the weather and not to the vein, and that the Hall will not keep it. Here the Keepers' rite and the older folk reverence first plainly part, and each side afterwards cites the ruling as proof that it was right.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-2041"><em>A hearth-elder puts the stream to Muireach</em>, 28 am Faoilleach, FE 52</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2045"></a>**24 an Cèitean, FE 64** — *Murchadh Mòr dies at Baile Mòr mhòr*. Murchadh Mòr, eldest of Ailean's living sons and the first knotted on Sìne's cord, dies at his own seat close on three thousand years old, having outlived every one of his generation but Eithne and a scattering of the youngest.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0098a"><em>Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, FE 1</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-2044"><em>Niall Òg sits an evening at Ceallach's hearth</em>, 4 an Dùbhlachd, FE 53</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2046"></a>**26 an Gearran, FE 65** — *Eleven knives for the north*. Murchadh Mòr's eleven sons, none by the same mother, divide the great share of the north among themselves with a knife to each of the north's chief holdings, over eleven nights of arguing which hall goes with which knife.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-II-0001b"><em>Roinn na Rìoghachd</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-2045"><em>Murchadh Mòr dies at Baile Mòr mhòr</em>, 24 an Cèitean, FE 64</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2047"></a>**27 am Màrt, FE 65** — *Lachlann Mòr takes Baile Mòr mhòr*. The eldest of Murchadh Mòr's eleven sons is given his father's own seat and its name with less argument than the rest of the division, none of his brothers wanting the weight of a hall so long held.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0001b"><em>Roinn na Rìoghachd</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-2046"><em>Eleven knives for the north</em>, 26 an Gearran, FE 65</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2048"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, FE 65** — *Donnchadh Iar disputes the western glens*. The fourth of Murchadh Mòr's sons wins the western glens only after the longest argument of the whole division, and goes on calling the settlement unjust for years after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0001b"><em>Roinn na Rìoghachd</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-2047"><em>Lachlann Mòr takes Baile Mòr mhòr</em>, 27 am Màrt, FE 65</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2049"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, FE 65** — *The north's counties too small for twenty spears*. What comes out of Baile Mòr mhòr's last division is a floor of small halls, none able to raise so much as twenty spears alone, a smallness the tellers already read as proof the long-lived blood was fading fastest from that line.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0001b"><em>Roinn na Rìoghachd</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0014"></a>**22 an Dàmhair, FE 66** — *The sick carried to Muileann ruadh* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). The sick are carried up in litters to the warm springs below Muileann ruadh and bathed at dawn. The Keepers allow it, for the heat of the water comes from the mountain and no one breaks the stone for it.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-2040"><em>Muireach walks up to Muileann ruadh</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, FE 49</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2050"></a>**24 an Cèitean, FE 67** — *Eachann Ruadh raids the Red Share's cattle*. Eachann Ruadh rides a dozen men across the boundary stones into the Red Share's northern grazing and drives off near forty head before the alarm is fully raised, the old feud from Dùn thais finding a fresh grievance to spend itself on.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-II-0001d"><em>Shares of shares</em>, 25 am Màrt, FE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2051"></a>**22 an t-Ògmhios, FE 67** — *Muireach refuses the Hall's ground to the cattle*. Asked to shelter the Red Share's recovered cattle on the Hall's own ground, Muireach Liath refuses, ruling that the ground was sworn to keep a man safe from a knife and never to make holy ground of every quarrel brought to his door.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-II-0001c"><em>First blood among the heirs</em>, 17 an Giblean, FE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2052"></a>**26 an Gearran, FE 69** — *A grey stone found apart from the vein* (Muileann chiar). A shepherd of the ninth hearth, hunting a ewe caught in bracken a few miles north of Dùn ìseal, finds a grey stone with a bright wound where her stick scraped the moss away and carries it down out of curiosity. It sits on a sill at Dùn ìseal a season, turned over by whoever passes, before anyone thinks to put fire to it.
- <a id="ev-EIII-2053"></a>**21 an t-Iuchar, FE 69** — *Fearchar Airgeadach smelts the first bead* (Muileann chiar). Fearchar, a basket-carrier of the ninth hearth who has spent three winters tending the vein's fires, builds his own fire apart from the Hall on the spur where the stone was found and feeds it through a day and half a night. Old Tormod, dozing beside him, wakes to find a bead of soft bright metal in Fearchar's hand that answers to no fire the Hall has ever kept.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-2052"><em>A grey stone found apart from the vein</em>, 26 an Gearran, FE 69</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2054"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, FE 69** — *Muileann chiar named* (Muileann chiar). Within a month Fearchar has raised a proper furnace of clay and dry stone on the spur and is hammering beads into rings. The households of the ninth hearth call the place Muileann chiar, the dark mill, after the smoke that hangs over it of a still morning, unmindful of the older place of that name far to the east.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-2053"><em>Fearchar Airgeadach smelts the first bead</em>, 21 an t-Iuchar, FE 69</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2055"></a>**28 am Faoilleach, FE 70** — *Muireach Liath rules the silver shows no blood* (Muileann chiar). Asked whether the new metal falls under the flame, Muireach Liath presses a ring's softest edge with his thumbnail, finds no colour beneath the break as a coal always shows, and rules that the Hall has no claim on a thing that shows no colour when it breaks. Fearchar is left free to dig on, and to keep or give what he digs.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-2054"><em>Muileann chiar named</em>, 19 an Lùnastal, FE 69</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0015"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, FE 71** — *Muileann chiar founded* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). A seam of silver is found near the great vein but apart from it. It is the first wealth of the island other than the coal.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-2052"><em>A grey stone found apart from the vein</em>, 26 an Gearran, FE 69</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2056"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, FE 71** — *The first ring set out for Goibhniu* (Muileann chiar). Fearchar takes up the custom of setting the first ring off every new furnace whole on a flat stone at the mouth of the workings, an offering to Goibhniu, before a second ring is begun. No furnace of his ever fails in its first season, which the smiths of Muileann chiar take as proof the god has taken the offerings kindly.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-2055"><em>Muireach Liath rules the silver shows no blood</em>, 28 am Faoilleach, FE 70</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0016"></a>**20 an t-Samhain, FE 74** — *Fearchar Airgeadach works the silver* (Muileann chiar). Fearchar Airgeadach, a basket-carrier of the nine hearths, is the first known to smelt the silver of Muileann chiar and hammer it into rings. His furnace burns wood and peat. It is the first fire on the island that answers to no one in the Hall.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-2053"><em>Fearchar Airgeadach smelts the first bead</em>, 21 an t-Iuchar, FE 69</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-2054"><em>Muileann chiar named</em>, 19 an Lùnastal, FE 69</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-2056"><em>The first ring set out for Goibhniu</em>, 6 an Dùbhlachd, FE 71</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0017"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, FE 74** — *Silver is not holy* (Muileann chiar). Asked whether the new seam falls under the flame, Muireach Liath answers that silver shows no colour when it breaks and so is not the mountain's. Muileann chiar is left free to dig as deep as it likes, and it digs. Every later quarrel over the silver begins from these words.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-2055"><em>Muireach Liath rules the silver shows no blood</em>, 28 am Faoilleach, FE 70</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2057"></a>**27 am Màrt, FE 75** — *Two cousins of the eastern share claim the silver ground* (Muileann chiar). Grandsons of one grandfather through different daughters, whose households have shared an unremarkable boundary along a dry burn since their grandfather's day, each send word to Dùn ìseal within days of the other, swearing the spur of Fearchar's furnaces lies on his own side of the burn. The keepers of the slab find the seam outside their reach to judge and send the cousins back to settle it themselves.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0017"><em>Silver is not holy</em>, 19 an Dùbhlachd, FE 74</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2058"></a>**9 an Gearran, FE 76** — *Fearchar pays a ring to each cousin* (Muileann chiar). Weary of digging under a dispute he did not start, Fearchar offers a ring from the season's working to each of the two cousins, on condition that both let the digging go on undisturbed while their elders argue the boundary. Both take the ring, neither gladly, and the quarrel is settled within the year by a boundary stone the two households cut and raise together at the driest point of the burn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0017"><em>Silver is not holy</em>, 19 an Dùbhlachd, FE 74</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-2057"><em>Two cousins of the eastern share claim the silver ground</em>, 27 am Màrt, FE 75</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2059"></a>**11 am Faoilleach, FE 77** — *The first ring traded at Ros fhionn* (Ros fhionn). A carrier of the ninth hearth strikes the first known trade of a ring against a whole boatload of salted fish and sealskin at the river quays of Ros fhionn. The measure holds for every later bargain on the quay, so that a boatman naming a price says simply "a ring's worth" and is understood without further reckoning.
- <a id="ev-EIII-2060"></a>**7 an Gearran, FE 79** — *Death of Ceallach mac Ghille-Bhrìde*. Ceallach, who has kept the coal of the First Flame in the high valleys since his father Gille-Brìde's death, dies in his sleep at the age of a hundred and forty, the last of Somhairle's line in whom the long years still showed. His household carries the coal down to the Hall's own flame; his children leave the high valleys within the year and settle among the lower hearths.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-II-0015"><em>Muileann chiar founded</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, FE 71</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0018"></a>**28 an t-Ògmhios, FE 84** — *Silver for salt at Ros fhionn* (Ros fhionn). Carriers take rings of Muileann chiar down to the river quays at Ros fhionn and trade them for salt fish and sealskin, one ring for a boatload. It is the first trade in anything but food, and the first whose price is remembered.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-2059"><em>The first ring traded at Ros fhionn</em>, 11 am Faoilleach, FE 77</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-2061"></a>**16 am Màrt, FE 89** — *Three candidates passed over for the flame* (Dùn ìseal). On Muireach Liath's death the nine hearths weigh three households' candidates at length: a steady grandson of the sixth hearth, a daughter of the third hearth whose grandmother helped choose Beathag Bhàn, and Muireach's own nephew of the ninth hearth. All three are passed over in favour of Muireach's daughter Gormshuil, chosen on the work alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-2060"><em>Death of Ceallach mac Ghille-Bhrìde</em>, 7 an Gearran, FE 79</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0019"></a>**30 an Cèitean, FE 89** — *Death of Muireach Liath* (Dùn ìseal). Muireach Liath dies at Dùn ìseal, keeping the flame. The nine hearths pass over three of other lines and choose his daughter Gormshuil nic Mhuirich. After her the Keeper's office stays in the house of Muireach for many generations.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-2061"><em>Three candidates passed over for the flame</em>, 16 am Màrt, FE 89</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3001"></a>**21 an t-Ògmhios, FE 89** — *Muireach's nephew goes to the furnaces* (Muileann chiar). Passed over for the flame on the strength of blood alone, Muireach Liath's nephew of the ninth hearth goes north within the year to take up work at one of Fearchar's furnaces at Muileann chiar, where he is said to prosper a good deal more than he might have as a Keeper chosen by kinship rather than by the households' own will.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0019"><em>Death of Muireach Liath</em>, 30 an Cèitean, FE 89</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-2061"><em>Three candidates passed over for the flame</em>, 16 am Màrt, FE 89</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0020"></a>**11 an t-Sultain, FE 96** — *Sliochd Mhuirich named* (Dùn ìseal). The kin of Gormshuil nic Mhuirich at Dùn ìseal begin to be called Sliochd Mhuirich, the house of Muireach, the first house of custody known by a name and not by a hearth. No account that survives tells of the other eight hearths objecting.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3002"></a>**13 an t-Iuchar, FE 97** — *Sìleas counts the coal's colours* (Muileann chiar). At the far-eastern Muileann chiar, Sìleas nic Coinnich begins counting which strokes of her own pick break the vein bright with colour and which break it plain dull coal, and notices the bright breaks come to no cutter's hand alone, not even her own, on every shift.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3003"></a>**14 an t-Ògmhios, FE 98** — *Sìleas's mother warns against the asking* (Muileann chiar). Sìleas's mother, who cut the same wall before her, tells her that a question put to the vein is better left unput, and that the mountain has fed the house four generations without being asked why. Sìleas holds her tongue, but not her counting.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3002"><em>Sìleas counts the coal's colours</em>, 13 an t-Iuchar, FE 97</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3004"></a>**9 an t-Sultain, FE 100** — *Sìleas moved from wall to wall* (Muileann chiar). The overseer of Muileann chiar's galleries, wearying of a cutter who tries the coal's answer against fasting, singing and the hour of the day, moves Sìleas nic Coinnich from wall to wall until no face is left that has not already been asked her questions.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3003"><em>Sìleas's mother warns against the asking</em>, 14 an t-Ògmhios, FE 98</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3005"></a>**11 an Lùnastal, FE 101** — *Sìleas withdraws to the holy wood* (Muileann chiar). Sìleas nic Coinnich goes up into Coille Naomh Muileann chiar meaning only to sit and think, and finds three cutters of her own galleries have followed her there unasked, each carrying the same unspoken question from the face.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3004"><em>Sìleas moved from wall to wall</em>, 9 an t-Sultain, FE 100</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0021"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, FE 103** — *The first school of the druids founded*. The first of the Scoiltean nan Draoidhean, the druid schools, gathers about one question: why the vein answers some hands and not others. For the first time within the Old Faith the coal is reasoned about, and not only revered.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3006"></a>**19 an t-Samhain, FE 103** — *Forty gather in the clearing* (Muileann chiar). Two springs after the first evening in the wood, near forty cutters, basket-carriers and children of the overseer's own house sit in the clearing above Muileann chiar to hear Sìleas nic Coinnich set out her counting, more than the old fallen trunk she taught from can seat.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3005"><em>Sìleas withdraws to the holy wood</em>, 11 an Lùnastal, FE 101</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0022"></a>**8 an t-Samhain, FE 110** — *Sìleas nic Coinnich in the wood* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). Sìleas nic Coinnich, a cutter from Muileann chiar in the far east, begins to teach in Coille Naomh Muileann chiar. At the galleries she had seen the coal break bright with its colours under some cutters' picks and dull under others, and she will not let the question be.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3002"><em>Sìleas counts the coal's colours</em>, 13 an t-Iuchar, FE 97</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-3003"><em>Sìleas's mother warns against the asking</em>, 14 an t-Ògmhios, FE 98</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-3004"><em>Sìleas moved from wall to wall</em>, 9 an t-Sultain, FE 100</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-3005"><em>Sìleas withdraws to the holy wood</em>, 11 an Lùnastal, FE 101</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3007"></a>**8 an Dàmhair, FE 112** — *A hearer walks a fortnight to the wood* (Muileann chiar). A woman of the northern shore, having heard a story of a stag grown taller with every telling between her home and the wood, walks a fortnight to sit in Sìleas's clearing, and is told plainly that the counting, not the stag, is the whole of what is taught there.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3006"><em>Forty gather in the clearing</em>, 19 an t-Samhain, FE 103</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0023"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, FE 118** — *The stag in the grove* (Muileann chiar). The hearers of Sìleas nic Coinnich at Muileann chiar name themselves the stag's people, for a stag said to have stood in the grove through a whole lesson. The school's later name, the stag's name Camaran, and the telling that it was the white stag of Flidais, lady of the deer, are found first in writings far younger than these days.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3006"><em>Forty gather in the clearing</em>, 19 an t-Samhain, FE 103</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-3007"><em>A hearer walks a fortnight to the wood</em>, 8 an Dàmhair, FE 112</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3008"></a>**3 am Faoilleach, FE 121** — *Ìomhar Dearg killed at the ford*. Riding to see a moved boundary stone on the Red Share's northern march, Ìomhar Dearg is speared through the throat at the ford of the Abhainn dhomhain by Eachann Ruadh mac Mhurchaidh, in payment for Aonghas Bàn's death at Dùn thais sixty years before. His riders bring him from the water dead.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0001b"><em>Roinn na Rìoghachd</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3009"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, FE 121** — *The Red Share held whole under Dùghall Dearg* (Dùn dhearg). Dùghall Dearg mac Ìomhair takes up the Red Share entire the week his father is buried, and tells the four lines who come to Dùn dhearg with old claims that the share was won with a sword and will be kept with one. None presses a claim against his household.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0001b"><em>Roinn na Rìoghachd</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3008"><em>Ìomhar Dearg killed at the ford</em>, 3 am Faoilleach, FE 121</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3010"></a>**9 an t-Ògmhios, FE 122** — *Eachann Ruadh flees to the Hall's ground* (Dùn ìseal). Eachann Ruadh mac Mhurchaidh rides through the night from the ford to the ground before the Hall of the Flame, throws down his second spear, and sits within sight of Brìde's fire until the Keeper's cutters come out to him, asking the ground and nothing of the flame itself.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-II-0022"><em>Sìleas nic Coinnich in the wood</em>, 8 an t-Samhain, FE 110</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3009"><em>The Red Share held whole under Dùghall Dearg</em>, 5 an Dùbhlachd, FE 121</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3011"></a>**8 an t-Iuchar, FE 122** — *Gormshuil rules the Hall's ground holds even a killer* (Dùn ìseal). Gormshuil nic Mhuirich rules that no spear may follow Eachann Ruadh mac Mhurchaidh past the Hall's boundary stone, though what waits for him beyond it is not hers to answer for, and lets him raise a hut at the ground's edge to cut turf for the Hall's own fires.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0022"><em>Sìleas nic Coinnich in the wood</em>, 8 an t-Samhain, FE 110</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3010"><em>Eachann Ruadh flees to the Hall's ground</em>, 9 an t-Ògmhios, FE 122</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3012"></a>**12 an Giblean, FE 123** — *A loaned cutter's report reaches Gormshuil* (Dùn ìseal). A cutter of Dùn ìseal's own galleries, home from a season's loan to Muileann chiar, tells the Hall in passing that the eastern cutters count their strokes and ask why the coal answers one hand and not another. Gormshuil sends her own cutter east to see the wood for herself.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0023"><em>The stag in the grove</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, FE 118</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3011"><em>Gormshuil rules the Hall's ground holds even a killer</em>, 8 an t-Iuchar, FE 122</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3013"></a>**11 an Cèitean, FE 124** — *Sìleas summoned to Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). Gormshuil nic Mhuirich summons Sìleas nic Coinnich to Dùn ìseal, and the two speak alone in the keepers' hut by the flame Beathag Bhàn once held. Neither afterwards gives a full account of what passed between them; only the ruling that follows is known.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3012"><em>A loaned cutter's report reaches Gormshuil</em>, 12 an Giblean, FE 123</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0024"></a>**18 an Cèitean, FE 125** — *The Hall shuts the galleries to the stag's people* (Dùn ìseal). Gormshuil nic Mhuirich forbids the hearers of Sìleas to cut in the galleries of Dùn ìseal, holding that a question asked of the vein is a demand made of it. The stag's people keep their school in the east and send no cutters to the mountain for a long while after.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3013"><em>Sìleas summoned to Dùn ìseal</em>, 11 an Cèitean, FE 124</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3014"></a>**22 an t-Samhain, FE 125** — *The eastern cutters walk further into the hills* (Muileann chiar). After the galleries of Dùn ìseal are shut to them, a dozen of Sìleas nic Coinnich's oldest hearers walk east out of Muileann chiar to raise a house of their own further from the mountain's shadow, following the wood where it thickens and the seam where it runs deeper.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0024"><em>The Hall shuts the galleries to the stag's people</em>, 18 an Cèitean, FE 125</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3013"><em>Sìleas summoned to Dùn ìseal</em>, 11 an Cèitean, FE 124</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3015"></a>**14 am Màrt, FE 127** — *Gormshuil nic Mhuirich dies at Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). Gormshuil, Keeper after Muireach Liath for thirty-eight years, dies in the small room off the Hall at the age of eighty-seven, her cutter's daughter and Fionnlagh Dall at her bedside. Her last words are a complaint about the cold of the room rather than any ruling, and the household keeps the telling of it fondly afterward.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0024"><em>The Hall shuts the galleries to the stag's people</em>, 18 an Cèitean, FE 125</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3016"></a>**15 am Faoilleach, FE 128** — *Fionnlagh Dall chosen Keeper* (Dùn ìseal). The nine hearths choose Fionnlagh, blind since a childhood fever and a sitter with the flame for thirty years, over a cutter of the fourth hearth and Gormshuil's own niece, on the argument of the niece's household that his hands judge a measure more truly than a sighted man's. He is thirty-eight years old, the first blind Keeper the island has known.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0024"><em>The Hall shuts the galleries to the stag's people</em>, 18 an Cèitean, FE 125</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3015"><em>Gormshuil nic Mhuirich dies at Dùn ìseal</em>, 14 am Màrt, FE 127</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3017"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, FE 128** — *Calum Beag begins leading the blind Keeper* (Dùn ìseal). A boy of ten who has followed Fionnlagh about the Hall since he could walk is brought to him by his own mother and asked to guide him through the galleries, on the one condition that he keep a Keeper's silence about what he sees there. He agrees at once, and the two go about Dùn ìseal together from that day.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3016"><em>Fionnlagh Dall chosen Keeper</em>, 15 am Faoilleach, FE 128</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3018"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, FE 131** — *A household at Cnoc dhubh burns by the basketful* (Cnoc dhubh). In a bitter winter a household of the high ground above Cnoc dhubh, its measured handful not enough to warm three children and an old woman through the worst nights, burns the coal by the basketful instead, a measure no household has burned before. The smoke lies down in the still valley air and will not lift.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3017"><em>Calum Beag begins leading the blind Keeper</em>, 17 an Dùbhlachd, FE 128</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0025"></a>**16 an t-Ògmhios, FE 132** — *The smoke at Cnoc dhubh* (Cnoc dhubh). In a hard winter a household at Cnoc dhubh burns its coal by the basketful and not by the handful. The smoke settles in the valley, and three of the household and two neighbours die of it. The Keepers are sent for, and the case is argued at Dùn ìseal for the rest of the season.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-3018"><em>A household at Cnoc dhubh burns by the basketful</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, FE 131</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3019"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, FE 132** — *Five die of the smoke at Cnoc dhubh* (Cnoc dhubh). Three of the burning household, a grandmother of the house beside it, and a neighbour's infant carried past the settling smoke are dead within three nights. Calum Beag carries the word to Fionnlagh, who goes up to the valley himself before any council is called.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0025"><em>The smoke at Cnoc dhubh</em>, 16 an t-Ògmhios, FE 132</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3018"><em>A household at Cnoc dhubh burns by the basketful</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, FE 131</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3020"></a>**30 an Dàmhair, FE 132** — *The season of argument at Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). The dead household's kin argue that a law which lets a house freeze rather than burn what the mountain holds in plenty is no law worth keeping; the other eight hearths, frightened by what one family's basketful did to two houses that burned nothing at all, argue the measure must hold unargued or hold not at all. Fionnlagh gives no ruling for the better part of two months.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0025"><em>The smoke at Cnoc dhubh</em>, 16 an t-Ògmhios, FE 132</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3019"><em>Five die of the smoke at Cnoc dhubh</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, FE 132</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3021"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, FE 138** — *Calum Beag finds the grey stone* (Dùn ìseal). Sent into the hills above Dùn ìseal to find stone hard, fine-grained and free of any crack, Calum Beag returns three days later with a cutter of the fourth hearth and a slab slung between two poles. Fionnlagh spends the better part of a month testing it by hand before he lets the chisel near it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3020"><em>The season of argument at Dùn ìseal</em>, 30 an Dàmhair, FE 132</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3022"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, FE 138** — *The stone cup cut to two palms* (Dùn ìseal). Fionnlagh has the new cup cut hollow to the exact measure of his own two hands cupped together, palm to palm, trusting his own hands to be the one instrument that never changes. He tests the fill again and again by touch alone until he can judge a hair's difference against the stone's cold lip.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3021"><em>Calum Beag finds the grey stone</em>, 19 an Lùnastal, FE 138</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0026"></a>**15 an t-Iuchar, FE 139** — *Fionnlagh Dall and the stone cup* (Dùn ìseal). Fionnlagh Dall, Keeper after Gormshuil, has the old keepers' stone cup cut anew in grey stone to hold just what a cupped pair of hands will hold, and sets it for the measure on the threshold of Talla na Lasrach at Dùn ìseal. He is blind, and fills it by touch before the council, and none can say afterwards that he favoured anyone's hands.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3016"><em>Fionnlagh Dall chosen Keeper</em>, 15 am Faoilleach, FE 128</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3017"><em>Calum Beag begins leading the blind Keeper</em>, 17 an Dùbhlachd, FE 128</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3020"><em>The season of argument at Dùn ìseal</em>, 30 an Dàmhair, FE 132</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3021"><em>Calum Beag finds the grey stone</em>, 19 an Lùnastal, FE 138</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-3022"><em>The stone cup cut to two palms</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, FE 138</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3023"></a>**9 an Dàmhair, FE 139** — *The cup set on the threshold* (Dùn ìseal). Rather than keep the new cup within the Hall where a favoured keeper's hand might reach it first, Fionnlagh sets it on the worn threshold stone of Talla na Lasrach, in the open, where any household or its neighbour can see the measure given. He finds the threshold's true centre by walking it barefoot.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0026"><em>Fionnlagh Dall and the stone cup</em>, 15 an t-Iuchar, FE 139</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3022"><em>The stone cup cut to two palms</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, FE 138</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3024"></a>**15 an Dàmhair, FE 139** — *An old woman of the fourth hearth trusts the measure* (Dùn ìseal). The first household to bring its claim to the new cup is a poor one, its elder's hands shaking with palsy. Fionnlagh fills the cup by touch, says "Enough" when the measure is met, and closes his hand over its lip. She weeps at a fairness she says she has not trusted from a sighted keeper in three years.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0026"><em>Fionnlagh Dall and the stone cup</em>, 15 an t-Iuchar, FE 139</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3023"><em>The cup set on the threshold</em>, 9 an Dàmhair, FE 139</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3025"></a>**19 an Cèitean, FE 142** — *The lords swear the Small-Burning Law* (Dùn ìseal). At the Samhain gathering the lords of every share, grumbling but pressed by the memory of Cnoc dhubh and the weeping woman of the fourth hearth, swear the measured handful into a law binding on every share alike, each laying a hand on the stone cup itself. It is the first law the island has ever kept the same in every share.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3024"><em>An old woman of the fourth hearth trusts the measure</em>, 15 an Dàmhair, FE 139</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0027"></a>**13 an Lùnastal, FE 142** — *The Small-Burning Law*. The custom of the handful is made law: no household may burn more than a measured handful of the coal in a season. It becomes the holy law of the Keepers of Brìde's flame and Crom's stone, and it holds for centuries.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3025"><em>The lords swear the Small-Burning Law</em>, 19 an Cèitean, FE 142</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0028"></a>**1 an Cèitean, FE 145** — *The first sentence under the Law* (Seann Tarr). A household of Seann Tarr burns twice its measure in a season and loses its right to the coal for the season after, the first sentence given under the Small-Burning Law. Its name is set on the roll with the offence beside it, and for many centuries its descendants petition to have the offence struck out.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3026"></a>**21 an Lùnastal, FE 145** — *Seann Tarr sentenced under the new law* (Seann Tarr). A fishing household of Seann Tarr, its catch ruined by wet weather, burns twice its measure to save its dried fish and is the first sentenced under the Small-Burning Law: it loses its right to the coal for the season following, its name and offence set on the roll. Fionnlagh gives the ruling with real reluctance.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0028"><em>The first sentence under the Law</em>, 1 an Cèitean, FE 145</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3025"><em>The lords swear the Small-Burning Law</em>, 19 an Cèitean, FE 142</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3027"></a>**1 an Giblean, FE 148** — *The question of the beacon at Tobar dhearg* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). A fisherman of the southern coast asks the council whether a beacon lit to warn strangers off the rocks, and no household's own hearth, should be counted against a household's handful at all. Fionnlagh takes the better part of a day alone with the stone cup before he answers.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3026"><em>Seann Tarr sentenced under the new law</em>, 21 an Lùnastal, FE 145</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0029"></a>**30 an Cèitean, FE 148** — *No coal on the beacons* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). The Keepers rule that no coal may feed a beacon, since a beacon burns for strangers. The fire on the headland at Tobar dhearg is kept with driftwood and seal fat, and so are all the sea-lights of the island after it.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3027"><em>The question of the beacon at Tobar dhearg</em>, 1 an Giblean, FE 148</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3028"></a>**14 an t-Sultain, FE 148** — *Driftwood and seal fat light the sea-lights* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). Fionnlagh rules that no coal may feed a beacon meant for strangers, since the vein answers to the island's own and to no boat that might never touch its shore. The beacon at Tobar dhearg is kept after with driftwood and rendered seal fat, and every sea-light raised on the island after it is kept the same way.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0029"><em>No coal on the beacons</em>, 30 an Cèitean, FE 148</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3027"><em>The question of the beacon at Tobar dhearg</em>, 1 an Giblean, FE 148</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3029"></a>**28 am Faoilleach, FE 149** — *Ailean Clachair takes on the steps to Ceann chaol* (Ceann chaol). The council at Dùn ìseal asks the nine hearths' cutters whether any will cut a proper path down the steep mile above the harbour of Ceann chaol, where carriers going down sideways on bare rock have turned more ankles than the Hall has troubled to count. Ailean Clachair, a cutter of the fourth hearth four and twenty years old, steps forward first.
- <a id="ev-II-0030"></a>**4 am Màrt, FE 151** — *The carriers' path to Ceann chaol* (Ceann chaol). A carriers' path is cut from the mountain down to the harbour of Ceann chaol, with steps hewn at the steep places. The Hall's baskets go down it to the southern households, and the dried fish of the south comes up.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3029"><em>Ailean Clachair takes on the steps to Ceann chaol</em>, 28 am Faoilleach, FE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3030"></a>**23 an Dàmhair, FE 151** — *The steps to Ceann chaol are finished* (Ceann chaol). After two years of work by Ailean Clachair and six others of the fourth hearth, the stepped path down to the harbour of Ceann chaol is finished, cut stone where the rock allows a step and fitted stone where it does not. A carrier with a full basket can go down to the harbour on a wet morning without setting a hand to the rock.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0030"><em>The carriers' path to Ceann chaol</em>, 4 am Màrt, FE 151</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3029"><em>Ailean Clachair takes on the steps to Ceann chaol</em>, 28 am Faoilleach, FE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3031"></a>**7 am Faoilleach, FE 154** — *Eleven carriers drown at the ford of the Abhainn dhomhain*. A party of eleven carriers bound south with the Hall's baskets crosses the ford of the Abhainn dhomhain on a night of hard rain, led by Beathag nan Cliabh on her own word that the rising water looks no worse than a flood she remembers from her youth. The river rises over a tall man's head before the last of them is across; only the one carrier who turned back at the water's edge survives to carry word of it.
- <a id="ev-II-0031"></a>**3 an Gearran, FE 154** — *The carriers drowned on the Abhainn dhomhain* (Abhainn dhomhain). The Abhainn dhomhain rises in the night and takes eleven carriers and their baskets at a ford. The Hall mourns the coal with the carriers, and Fionnlagh Dall asks the council for a way across that the river cannot take.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3031"><em>Eleven carriers drown at the ford of the Abhainn dhomhain</em>, 7 am Faoilleach, FE 154</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3032"></a>**27 an Giblean, FE 154** — *The Hall sets the names of the drowned upon its roll* (Dùn ìseal). Fionnlagh Dall has the eleven names read to him twice before he will let the roll be closed, among them Beathag nan Cliabh, Griogair mac Ailig, Sìneag nighean Dhonnchaidh, and a boy the roll gives only as young Tormod of the salt shore, who went on the crossing in place of an uncle whose knee had gone bad in the wet.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0031"><em>The carriers drowned on the Abhainn dhomhain</em>, 3 an Gearran, FE 154</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3033"></a>**14 an Lùnastal, FE 154** — *The carriers' joke of the mourned coal*. The carriers who come after the drowning make a joke of their own grief, saying the Hall mourns its coal along with its dead, since eleven baskets went into the river with the eleven who carried them. Fionnlagh, hearing it repeated to him, does not rebuke it, and says a mountain that measures its coal so carefully may be allowed to grieve a basketful lost the same way its people grieve a life.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0031"><em>The carriers drowned on the Abhainn dhomhain</em>, 3 an Gearran, FE 154</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3032"><em>The Hall sets the names of the drowned upon its roll</em>, 27 an Giblean, FE 154</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3034"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, FE 154** — *Fionnlagh asks the council for a crossing the river cannot take* (Dùn ìseal). Fionnlagh brings the drowning before the council within the fortnight and asks for a crossing the Abhainn dhomhain cannot take in any weather. An elder of the southern hearths argues the river's risk is no worse than any ordinary misfortune; Fionnlagh answers that he asked only whether the risk could be made smaller, and asks who can name him a mason proved against water and weight.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0031"><em>The carriers drowned on the Abhainn dhomhain</em>, 3 an Gearran, FE 154</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3033"><em>The carriers' joke of the mourned coal</em>, 14 an Lùnastal, FE 154</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3035"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, FE 155** — *Ailean Clachair is charged with the crossing at Ros fhionn* (Drochaid Ros fhionn). The council calls Ailean Clachair, whose steps above Ceann chaol a wet winter has not yet broken, and charges him with a single stone span above Ros fhionn, where the river runs narrower and its banks stand higher and firmer than anywhere else along its reach. Ailean answers that he does not know whether such a span can be built at all, but will try rather than tell a Keeper who has just buried eleven carriers that it cannot.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3034"><em>Fionnlagh asks the council for a crossing the river cannot take</em>, 5 an Dùbhlachd, FE 154</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3036"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, FE 156** — *Ailean gathers the forty of the nine hearths* (Ros fhionn). Over a winter Ailean draws forty cutters and masons from the nine hearths, none of whom has ever cut anything meant to hold a river's weight rather than a roof's. They quarry grey stone near Ros fhionn and spend a season learning how stone cut to a wedge's shape leans upon its neighbours and holds itself up by leaning.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3035"><em>Ailean Clachair is charged with the crossing at Ros fhionn</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, FE 155</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0032"></a>**5 am Faoilleach, FE 157** — *The first bridges* (Drochaid Cathair dhearg). Stone crossings begin to join the mining paths of the interior to the coast. From them in time come Drochaid Cathair dhearg and Drochaid Ros fhionn.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3037"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, FE 158** — *Aonghas Beag falls on the centring* (Drochaid Ros fhionn). In the sixth week of the building, a mason of the ninth hearth named Aonghas Beag puts a foot wrong on wet timber and is caught at the edge of the fall by two others. Ailean keeps him off the scaffold for two days, saying a mason frightened in his own body cuts stone worse than one who has never learned fear.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3036"><em>Ailean gathers the forty of the nine hearths</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, FE 156</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0033"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, FE 160** — *Ailean Clachair's crossing at Ros fhionn* (Drochaid Ros fhionn). Ailean Clachair and forty masons of the nine hearths bridge the river above Ros fhionn with a single span of fitted stone, from which Drochaid Ros fhionn descends. Ailean sets a hearth-sign in the keystone. Every bridge the masons build after bears one, and a bridge without it is not trusted.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3034"><em>Fionnlagh asks the council for a crossing the river cannot take</em>, 5 an Dùbhlachd, FE 154</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3035"><em>Ailean Clachair is charged with the crossing at Ros fhionn</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, FE 155</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3036"><em>Ailean gathers the forty of the nine hearths</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, FE 156</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3037"><em>Aonghas Beag falls on the centring</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, FE 158</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3038"></a>**8 an Dùbhlachd, FE 160** — *The single span above Ros fhionn is closed* (Drochaid Ros fhionn). The keystone is raised on ropes and levers and set into the arch above Ros fhionn, Ailean himself guiding it the last hand's-width into place while the forty stand silent on both banks. The scaffold comes down within the week and the span stands alone over the water on its own weight and shape.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0033"><em>Ailean Clachair's crossing at Ros fhionn</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, FE 160</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3037"><em>Aonghas Beag falls on the centring</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, FE 158</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3039"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, FE 160** — *Ailean cuts the first hearth-sign in a keystone* (Drochaid Ros fhionn). Before the scaffold comes down, Ailean cuts the fourth hearth's own mark into the keystone's face, unasked, so that any eye that looks for it may know the stone was raised by hands that answer for their own work. The mark spreads to every span the forty raise after, and within a handful of years a crossing without it is said, not always fairly, to be a crossing built by hands that had not troubled to answer for themselves.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0033"><em>Ailean Clachair's crossing at Ros fhionn</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, FE 160</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3038"><em>The single span above Ros fhionn is closed</em>, 8 an Dùbhlachd, FE 160</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3040"></a>**5 an Dàmhair, FE 161** — *The masons swear the oath of the stone cup* (Dùn ìseal). Gathered at Dùn ìseal to be paid for the season's labour, the forty ask Fionnlagh whether they may swear a fellowship of their own. Each lays a hand on the stone cup at the threshold of Talla na Lasrach and swears that no span will ever be closed to a traveller in the dark, and none ever paid for in coal.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3039"><em>Ailean cuts the first hearth-sign in a keystone</em>, 19 an Dùbhlachd, FE 160</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0034"></a>**8 an t-Samhain, FE 163** — *The masons' custom* (Ros dhomhain). The bridge-masons form a fellowship bound by an oath sworn on the stone cup at Dùn ìseal: no span to be closed in the dark, and none to be paid for in coal. Their lodge is kept near the western crossing, in the country of Ros dhomhain.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3039"><em>Ailean cuts the first hearth-sign in a keystone</em>, 19 an Dùbhlachd, FE 160</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-3040"><em>The masons swear the oath of the stone cup</em>, 5 an Dàmhair, FE 161</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3041"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, FE 163** — *The masons' lodge is raised at the western crossing* (Ros dhomhain). Having kept together under Ailean's leading and raised three crossings more, the forty build a plain stone lodge beside the widest of the three, above a badly-used ford in the country of Ros dhomhain, where a mason called from any share may find a roof, a fire, and a fellow of the trade.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0034"><em>The masons' custom</em>, 8 an t-Samhain, FE 163</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3040"><em>The masons swear the oath of the stone cup</em>, 5 an Dàmhair, FE 161</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3042"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, FE 163** — *A carrier refuses an unsigned bridge* (Ros dhomhain). A cart-builder of Ros dhomhain throws an unmarked crossing of his own upriver of the western span. A carrier of the Hall's baskets, reaching it after dark, will not cross it, saying he knows whose oath a bridge without the fourth hearth's sign was not built under, and sleeps cold on the near bank rather than trust it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0034"><em>The masons' custom</em>, 8 an t-Samhain, FE 163</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3041"><em>The masons' lodge is raised at the western crossing</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, FE 163</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3043"></a>**3 an t-Samhain, FE 164** — *Mòr nic Dhùghaill feeds three carriers in the rain* (Doire shean). A widow of Doire shean with more buffalo than grass boils a haunch for three carriers caught by a mud-slicked path, and asks no coin for it. Word of the free bowl travels the mountain road faster than any basket on it, and within a year she has built a second room to feed the men it sends her.
- <a id="ev-II-0035"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, FE 166** — *The tavern roads begin* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). The first waypoint houses are raised along the mining roads. From them come in time Am Buabhall Fortanach, An Taigh-òsta Grianach and the others of the circuit.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3043"><em>Mòr nic Dhùghaill feeds three carriers in the rain</em>, 3 an t-Samhain, FE 164</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3044"></a>**11 an t-Ògmhios, FE 168** — *The turf longhouse raised at the crossing*. Three families of the fourth hearth build a long turf house where the mountain road meets the road to the western harbours, a hearth burning at either end for carriers going up and carriers coming down. Its long central table becomes the place where news of the whole road first gathers as one telling.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3043"><em>Mòr nic Dhùghaill feeds three carriers in the rain</em>, 3 an t-Samhain, FE 164</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0036"></a>**11 an t-Sultain, FE 169** — *Mòr nic Dhùghaill's house* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). Mòr nic Dhùghaill, a widow of Doire shean, keeps the first waypoint house on the site of Am Buabhall Fortanach. She serves the carriers jugged buffalo from her own herd, and the house has served it ever since.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-3043"><em>Mòr nic Dhùghaill feeds three carriers in the rain</em>, 3 an t-Samhain, FE 164</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3045"></a>**13 an Cèitean, FE 170** — *Seann Mhorn resettled and its name kept* (Seann Mhorn). Fishers of the nine hearths find old house-footings above a good landing on the western shore of Loch chrom, and a name already fixed to the place that is not of their own tongue. They keep the name rather than giving it a new one, judging that a name found standing has more right to stay than one a stranger could invent.
- <a id="ev-II-0037"></a>**13 an Lùnastal, FE 172** — *The house at the middle of the road* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). A second waypoint house is built where the carriers' road from the mountain meets the road to the western harbours, on the site of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr. It is a turf longhouse with a hearth at either end, one for carriers going up and one for carriers coming down.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-3044"><em>The turf longhouse raised at the crossing</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, FE 168</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3046"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, FE 172** — *Seann Warr resettled beside it* (Seann Warr). Families walking the same road find a second harbour a short way along the shore, house-footings there as well, and build on them without asking whose. Seann Warr and Seann Mhorn grow together within the century, sharing a landing, a market day and a single waypoint house where the mountain road meets the sea.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3047"></a>**7 an Cèitean, FE 175** — *A chase stopped at Mòr's door* (Doire shean). A man fleeing his cousin's kin over an old knife-wound takes shelter at Mòr nic Dhùghaill's table, and his three pursuers, knives at their belts, find her standing between them and the fire. She swears there will be no blade drawn under her roof for any grievance, old or new, and feeds all four from the one pot until the debt walks back out onto the open road unsettled between them.
- <a id="ev-II-0038"></a>**22 an Dàmhair, FE 175** — *The road-peace* (An Sligeanach Fad' às). The keepers of the waypoint houses agree that no feud may be pursued under an inn roof or within a spear's throw of its door. The custom is first set down at the house on the site of An Sligeanach Fad' às. It is the oldest law on the island that neither Keeper nor lord made.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3047"><em>A chase stopped at Mòr's door</em>, 7 an Cèitean, FE 175</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3048"></a>**15 an Gearran, FE 176** — *The road-peace kept as custom*. Word of the chase stopped at Mòr's door runs the mountain road faster than any basket that season, and other waypoint houses along the circuit take up the same custom unasked: no feud pursued and no blade drawn under a road-house roof or within a spear's throw of its door.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0038"><em>The road-peace</em>, 22 an Dàmhair, FE 175</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3047"><em>A chase stopped at Mòr's door</em>, 7 an Cèitean, FE 175</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3049"></a>**17 am Faoilleach, FE 177** — *Niall Òg sits at Mòr's table* (Doire shean). The old heir Niall Òg walks the mountain road to see for himself the house where a widow's word held two feuding kin to one table, and is given the same bowl and the same seat as any other traveller. He leaves a ring behind that Mòr will not keep, saying a man who has outlived his own quarrels can afford, once in a while, to pay for a peace he did not make.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0038"><em>The road-peace</em>, 22 an Dàmhair, FE 175</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3048"><em>The road-peace kept as custom</em>, 15 an Gearran, FE 176</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0039"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, FE 178** — *Seann Mhorn resettled* (Seann Mhorn). Fishers of the nine hearths settle the harbour at Seann Mhorn and keep the name they find there, which is not of their own tongue; the old name came with the stones, they say. It is the first such name known to be taken over and not replaced.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-3045"><em>Seann Mhorn resettled and its name kept</em>, 13 an Cèitean, FE 170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0040"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, FE 181** — *Seann Warr resettled* (Seann Warr). Families walking the new road from the mountain settle the harbour of Seann Warr on the western shore of Loch chrom in like manner. They find house-footings there already, and build on them, as the carriers' song has it, without asking whose.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-3046"><em>Seann Warr resettled beside it</em>, 11 an t-Samhain, FE 172</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0041"></a>**23 an Lùnastal, FE 184** — *Death of Fionnlagh Dall* (Dùn ìseal). Fionnlagh Dall dies at Dùn ìseal. At his own asking he is not laid on the slope with the Keepers before him, but carried south to the old graves near Cnoc dhìreach, which no living people had yet claimed.
- <a id="ev-II-0042"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, FE 184** — *Fionnlagh Dall carried to the old graves* (Tuam Cnoc dhìreach). The bearers are eleven days on the road with the body of Fionnlagh Dall, and lay it at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach among graves older than any name. The Keepers after him cannot agree why he asked it; two answers are given, and neither is chosen.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3050"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, FE 184** — *Fionnlagh Dall asks to be carried south* (Dùn ìseal). Dying at four-and-ninety after fifty-six years keeping the flame, Fionnlagh Dall tells Calum Beag he wishes to be laid not on the Keepers' own slope but in the unclaimed old graves near Cnoc dhìreach, ground no household's cord has ever divided. He dies within the month, his last words a question about whether the flame had been fed.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0041"><em>Death of Fionnlagh Dall</em>, 23 an Lùnastal, FE 184</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3051"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, FE 184** — *The eleven days' bearing* (Doire shean). Bearers carry Fionnlagh Dall's body the twenty miles to Cnoc dhìreach in eleven days rather than three, as every hearth on the road asks to carry him some part of the way. Calum Beag walks the whole distance at the litter's head, the only bearer who never once hands off his own share of the weight.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0042"><em>Fionnlagh Dall carried to the old graves</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, FE 184</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3050"><em>Fionnlagh Dall asks to be carried south</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, FE 184</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3052"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, FE 184** — *Tuam Cnoc dhìreach hallowed* (Cnoc dhìreach). Fionnlagh Dall is laid in the ancient, unclaimed burying-ground near Cnoc dhìreach, the first burial there any living hand has set down by name. The Keepers hallow the ground that same season, and it passes from belonging to no one to belonging, by the Hall's own reckoning, to everyone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3051"><em>The eleven days' bearing</em>, 12 an Dùbhlachd, FE 184</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3053"></a>**16 am Màrt, FE 185** — *The grave-keepers of Cnoc dhìreach paid in coal* (Cnoc dhìreach). A handful of families settle by Tuam Cnoc dhìreach to tend the grave, and the Hall pays them one measured handful of coal each a season, the only service the Small-Burning Law is ever known to reward in coal rather than coin or kind.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3052"><em>Tuam Cnoc dhìreach hallowed</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, FE 184</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3054"></a>**8 an Lùnastal, FE 186** — *Mòr nic Dhùghaill dies at her own hearth* (Doire shean). Found sitting upright in her fireside chair one morning by her own daughter, Mòr nic Dhùghaill dies at sixty-two, two years after Fionnlagh Dall. Her daughter and a niece take up the pot the same week, and the house does not miss a single night's fire.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0036"><em>Mòr nic Dhùghaill's house</em>, 11 an t-Sultain, FE 169</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0043"></a>**21 an t-Sultain, FE 189** — *The mausoleum consecrated*. Tuam Cnoc dhìreach, already ancient, is hallowed by the Keepers over the grave of Fionnlagh Dall, the first burial there that is set down by name. The burial-ground that no one claimed is claimed.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-3052"><em>Tuam Cnoc dhìreach hallowed</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, FE 184</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3055"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, FE 189** — *Calum Beag sets a marker at the grave* (Cnoc dhìreach). Calum Beag, now an old man, carries a plain stone the whole way to Cnoc dhìreach on his own back and sets it at Fionnlagh Dall's grave-head with his own hands, cut with nothing but the shape of the stone cup and no name, judging the shape said enough on its own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0043"><em>The mausoleum consecrated</em>, 21 an t-Sultain, FE 189</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0044"></a>**26 an t-Ògmhios, FE 194** — *The grave-keepers of Cnoc dhìreach* (Cnoc dhìreach). A few families settle at Cnoc dhìreach to tend Tuam Cnoc dhìreach after the Keeper's burial. The Hall pays them in coal, a handful each a season, the only payment in coal the Law ever allows.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-3053"><em>The grave-keepers of Cnoc dhìreach paid in coal</em>, 16 am Màrt, FE 185</a>.</span>

## The Years FE 201 – 400

- <a id="ev-EIII-3056"></a>**11 an t-Ògmhios, FE 214** — *The wedding insult at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). At a mason's wedding on the western share, Griogair mac Lachlainn of Sliochd Fhionnghail strikes Tormod mac Ruairidh of Sliochd Artair across the face with a drinking-horn after a slight against Fionnghal nic Ailein's memory. Both men are dragged from the hall still nursing the insult, and the two lines that had traded fish for grain for three generations begin refusing each other's carriers at their waypoint houses.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3057"></a>**10 an t-Iuchar, FE 216** — *The first raid of the wedding quarrel* (Ros dhomhain). A dozen head of cattle are lifted from a salt-shore pasture by men who call it payment owed for the insult at Ros dhomhain. A barn burns on the western share's ground within the season in answer, and within five years neither line can say with certainty who struck first.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3056"><em>The wedding insult at Ros dhomhain</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, FE 214</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3058"></a>**25 an Lùnastal, FE 236** — *Eimhir nic Mhuirich chosen to keep the flame* (Dùn ìseal). The nine hearths choose Eimhir nic Mhuirich, of the hearth-line and past sixty already, to keep the flame at Dùn ìseal. She holds the Hall to its measure through the widening quarrel of the king's blood, judging no man's raids and taking no side between Sliochd Fhionnghail and Sliochd Artair.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3059"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, FE 245** — *Tormod mac Ruairidh asks the Hall's blessing on a raid* (Dùn ìseal). Tormod mac Ruairidh comes to Dùn ìseal asking Eimhir nic Mhuirich to bless a raid he calls justice rather than vengeance. She hears him out and refuses, telling him the Hall keeps coal and not grudges, and that the flame she keeps was lit before his own great-grandfather was born.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3058"><em>Eimhir nic Mhuirich chosen to keep the flame</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, FE 236</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3060"></a>**22 an Dàmhair, FE 262** — *Fionnghal nic Ailein dies* (Ros dhomhain). Fionnghal nic Ailein, daughter of Ailean Mòr and holder of the western share since the age's early years, dies at Ros dhomhain some two thousand eight hundred and forty-four years old. Her funeral is the last occasion on which Sliochd Fhionnghail and Sliochd Artair stand under one roof without a blow struck.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3061"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, FE 290** — *Eimhir nic Mhuirich dies* (Dùn ìseal). Eimhir nic Mhuirich dies at Dùn ìseal some eighty years old, having kept the flame through fifty-four years of the widening strife of the heirs more steadily than the quarrel's own principals kept their tempers. The nine hearths choose a younger Keeper who holds much the same course.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3062"></a>**25 an Lùnastal, FE 298** — *Artair mac Ailein dies* (Baile ghorm). Artair mac Ailein, son of Ailean Mòr and holder of the salt shore at Baile ghorm, dies at his own hall some two thousand six hundred years old, the widening feud between his own descendants and Fionnghal's a weight he carried into his last years and could not set down.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3063"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, FE 331** — *Cormac mac Ailein dies* (Caol shean). Cormac mac Ailein, son of Ailean Mòr and holder of the eastern share at Caol shean, dies some two thousand four hundred and fifty-three years old, the last of Ailean's own children still living at the strife's true middle. His last wish, that his household keep clear of the western quarrel, is honoured for less than a generation.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3062"><em>Artair mac Ailein dies</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, FE 298</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3064"></a>**28 an t-Ògmhios, FE 352** — *Niall Òg calls a peace at the crossing of Ros fhionn* (Cathair dhearg). Niall Òg sets a long table on neutral ground at the crossing of Ros fhionn and brings the heads of Sliochd Fhionnghail and Sliochd Artair to it unarmed, hoping to loosen a quarrel now two generations old. Each recites a longer account of wrongs than he came with, neither offers an apology, and both walk home by the same road they came by.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3063"><em>Cormac mac Ailein dies</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, FE 331</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3065"></a>**30 an Cèitean, FE 353** — *The raids resume after the failed peace*. Within the season of Niall Òg's failed peace at Ros fhionn, raids between Sliochd Fhionnghail and Sliochd Artair begin again, if indeed they had ever truly stopped for the meeting.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3064"><em>Niall Òg calls a peace at the crossing of Ros fhionn</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, FE 352</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-3066"></a>**1 an Cèitean, FE 360** — *The tally-stick of Cnoc leathan* (Baile chiar). A household of the fourth hearth at Cnoc leathan, sworn to neither quarrelling line, keeps a tally-stick notched for whichever share's steward calls first each season. By the century's turn it carries better than a hundred and fifty notches on each face, a plainer record than either quarrelling line keeps of its own raids.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3067"></a>**2 an Giblean, FE 377** — *Eachann Ruadh mac Mhurchaidh dies in his bed* (Dùn ìseal). Eachann Ruadh mac Mhurchaidh, who killed Ìomhar Dearg at a ford four generations before in vengeance for his brother, dies quietly in his bed at seven hundred and twenty-nine years old, the last of his generation of the king's kin. His own line, long at peace with the Red Share, takes no fresh quarrel from his death.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3068"></a>**8 an Giblean, FE 381** — *The hearth-elders sound out Eilidh nic Ìomhair* (Dùn dhearg). Two elders of the nine hearths walk from Dùn ìseal to Dùn dhearg to ask Eilidh nic Ìomhair, a granddaughter's granddaughter of Ìomhar Dearg who keeps the Red Share's granary rolls, whether she would be persuaded to sit a season with the coal. She names the difficulty herself before they can raise it: her own blood.
- <a id="ev-EIII-3069"></a>**17 an Giblean, FE 381** — *Eilidh tells the elders to choose another* (Dùn dhearg). Eilidh nic Ìomhair tells the two hearth-elders plainly to choose one of the other names put forward, having no wish to force the question of her own blood against the Binding's old rule.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3068"><em>The hearth-elders sound out Eilidh nic Ìomhair</em>, 8 an Giblean, FE 381</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0045"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, FE 381** — *Eilidh nic Ìomhair keeps the flame* (Dùn ìseal). The nine hearths choose a Keeper from outside the house of Muireach for the first time: Eilidh nic Ìomhair, of Dùn dhearg, of the line of Ìomhar Dearg and so of the king's blood. Sliochd Mhuirich, holding to the Binding, refuses for a season, then yields at Dùn ìseal, on the condition that the stone cup never leaves Talla na Lasrach.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3068"><em>The hearth-elders sound out Eilidh nic Ìomhair</em>, 8 an Giblean, FE 381</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-3069"><em>Eilidh tells the elders to choose another</em>, 17 an Giblean, FE 381</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4001"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, FE 381** — *The Keeper before Eilidh dies at the cup* (Dùn ìseal). The Keeper who held the flame after Eimhir nic Mhuirich dies sitting on the low stool beside the stone cup at Talla na Lasrach, her hands folded in her lap. The small lamp beside her burns out unfed in the night, the first time in living memory that any lamp in the Hall has been let go dark.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-3069"><em>Eilidh tells the elders to choose another</em>, 17 an Giblean, FE 381</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4002"></a>**15 am Faoilleach, FE 382** — *The cup left unfilled a season* (Dùn ìseal). For the better part of a year after the nine hearths choose Eilidh, Sliochd Mhuirich refuses to yield the flame, and the stone cup at Talla na Lasrach sits under the care of the hearth-line's own eldest, unfilled by any new hand, while every market and threshing floor on the mountain airs an opinion on the matter.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0045"><em>Eilidh nic Ìomhair keeps the flame</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, FE 381</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4001"><em>The Keeper before Eilidh dies at the cup</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, FE 381</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4003"></a>**13 an Gearran, FE 382** — *The argument of the diluted blood* (Dùn dhearg). Eilidh's own kin argue to her, and to anyone who will listen, that half the households in the hills carry some thread of the king's blood by now, so that the Binding's old rule has become a rule against nearly everybody or nobody. Eilidh answers that the argument settles nothing Sliochd Mhuirich has actually asked.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0045"><em>Eilidh nic Ìomhair keeps the flame</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, FE 381</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4002"><em>The cup left unfilled a season</em>, 15 am Faoilleach, FE 382</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4004"></a>**8 an t-Iuchar, FE 382** — *The hearth-line eldest offers the cup's condition* (Dùn ìseal). The eldest of Sliochd Mhuirich comes to the Hall's threshold and offers a single condition for yielding the flame to Eilidh nic Ìomhair: that the stone cup Fionnlagh Dall cut to the measure of two palms shall never, for any cause, be carried out through the door of Talla na Lasrach.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0045"><em>Eilidh nic Ìomhair keeps the flame</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, FE 381</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4003"><em>The argument of the diluted blood</em>, 13 an Gearran, FE 382</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4005"></a>**6 an Lùnastal, FE 382** — *Eilidh swears to the cup's condition* (Dùn ìseal). Eilidh nic Ìomhair swears before the nine hearths that the stone cup will never leave Talla na Lasrach, her hand flat on its rim, and takes the coal that same afternoon, the measure poured level to her palm exactly as for every Keeper before her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4004"><em>The hearth-line eldest offers the cup's condition</em>, 8 an t-Iuchar, FE 382</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4006"></a>**1 am Faoilleach, FE 385** — *Sliochd Thormoid names Tormod Liath* (Dùn ìseal). At a gathering of the nine hearths, the eldest of Sliochd Thormoid names for the first time an ancestor called Tormod Liath, said to have held the hill itself under the old king, as the ground of the house's claim to a voice in the Keeper's office.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4007"></a>**26 am Faoilleach, FE 385** — *Sliochd Raghnaill names Raghnall Ceannfhionn* (Seann Tarr). Sliochd Raghnaill answers Sliochd Thormoid's claim with its own, naming an ancestor Raghnall Ceannfhionn, though the house rests its true weight less on any hill than on the plain fact that its boats carry more coal down the coast in a bad season than any other house's carts carry inland.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4006"><em>Sliochd Thormoid names Tormod Liath</em>, 1 am Faoilleach, FE 385</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4008"></a>**28 am Màrt, FE 385** — *Eilidh binds the office to four houses* (Dùn ìseal). Eilidh nic Ìomhair puts to the nine hearths that the Keeper's office be bound from that season to four houses of custody alone, Sliochd Mhuirich, Sliochd Ìomhair, Sliochd Thormoid and Sliochd Raghnaill, and that the other hearths keep their council seats but surrender any further claim on the flame.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4007"><em>Sliochd Raghnaill names Raghnall Ceannfhionn</em>, 26 am Faoilleach, FE 385</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0046"></a>**29 an Giblean, FE 385** — *The Four Houses sworn* (Dùn ìseal). Under Eilidh nic Ìomhair the office of Keeper is bound to four houses of custody: Sliochd Mhuirich of Dùn ìseal, Sliochd Ìomhair of Dùn dhearg, Sliochd Thormoid of Seann Dunn and Sliochd Raghnaill of Seann Tarr. The other hearths keep their seats on the council, but lose their claim to the flame. Most of the later nobility of the island descends from one of the four, or says it does.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4005"><em>Eilidh swears to the cup's condition</em>, 6 an Lùnastal, FE 382</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4006"><em>Sliochd Thormoid names Tormod Liath</em>, 1 am Faoilleach, FE 385</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4007"><em>Sliochd Raghnaill names Raghnall Ceannfhionn</em>, 26 am Faoilleach, FE 385</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4008"><em>Eilidh binds the office to four houses</em>, 28 am Màrt, FE 385</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4009"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, FE 386** — *The grumble over Seann Dunn's fullest lamp* (Seann Dunn). The other three houses grumble that Sliochd Thormoid's coal-lamp at Seann Dunn always burns fuller than the Law's measure allows, though no cutter sent to check it ever finds a grain over the handful. Eilidh judges the grievance one best left to wear out on its own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4008"><em>Eilidh binds the office to four houses</em>, 28 am Màrt, FE 385</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0047"></a>**28 an Cèitean, FE 389** — *The house of Tormod at Seann Dunn* (Seann Dunn). Sliochd Thormoid raises a hall and a shrine at Seann Dunn, facing the mountain across the river. A lamp of coal burns in the shrine at the Law's measure. The other houses complain that the measure of Seann Dunn is always the fullest.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-4009"><em>The grumble over Seann Dunn's fullest lamp</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, FE 386</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4010"></a>**1 an t-Samhain, FE 390** — *Sliochd Raghnaill grows rich on the fishing* (Seann Tarr). The house that took its seat at Seann Tarr, the very town first sentenced under the Small-Burning Law, keeps no galleries and cuts no coal, choosing boats instead, and grows rich enough within two generations that its neighbours stop mentioning the old offence.
- <a id="ev-II-0048"></a>**2 am Màrt, FE 393** — *The house of Raghnall at Seann Tarr* (Seann Tarr). Sliochd Raghnaill takes for its seat Seann Tarr on the north-eastern coast, the town whose household was first sentenced under the Law. The house keeps boats and not galleries, and grows rich on the fishing.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-4010"><em>Sliochd Raghnaill grows rich on the fishing</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 390</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4011"></a>**3 an Gearran, FE 397** — *The wager at Seann Tarr's quay* (Seann Tarr). Tormod Ruadh, a steersman of Sliochd Raghnaill, insists through a winter of evenings at Seann Tarr's quay that a boat could as easily be sailed round the black island Eilean dhubh as fished within sight of it, and finds himself, come spring, with a crew of four and a wager too large to back out of.
- <a id="ev-II-0049"></a>**31 am Màrt, FE 397** — *Round Eilean dhubh* (Eilean dhubh). Boats of Sliochd Raghnaill sail round Eilean dhubh and come home, the first voyage made to see a coast and not to fish it. The house's songs name the steersman Tormod Ruadh. He brings back word of rock and birds, and of having gone, and of nothing else.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4011"><em>The wager at Seann Tarr's quay</em>, 3 an Gearran, FE 397</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4012"></a>**11 an t-Ògmhios, FE 397** — *The strand mistakes Tormod Ruadh's boat for a stranger's*. A strand that has never before had reason to look for a boat of Seann Tarr's from that quarter of the sea sights Tormod Ruadh's boat rounding Eilean dhubh's far side and takes alarm at it, word of the strange sighting reaching Dùn ìseal well ahead of the boat's own return.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0049"><em>Round Eilean dhubh</em>, 31 am Màrt, FE 397</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4011"><em>The wager at Seann Tarr's quay</em>, 3 an Gearran, FE 397</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4013"></a>**6 an Lùnastal, FE 398** — *Murchadh Ruadh's household loses its right* (Baile chrom). The household of Murchadh Ruadh of Baile chrom is stripped of its right under the Law for a third offence, and goes down to the strand with what it can carry rather than beg cold porridge from kin. No hearth on the coast will give it coal after, or discuss why.

## The Years FE 401 – 600

- <a id="ev-II-0050"></a>**26 an t-Sultain, FE 401** — *The outlaws of the north-west waters* (Spùinneadairean-mara). Households stripped of their right under the Law for a third offence take to boats, live off the north-western waters, and raid the fishing strands. They are called spùinneadairean, plunderers, and the name stays with those waters after them.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4013"><em>Murchadh Ruadh's household loses its right</em>, 6 an Lùnastal, FE 398</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4014"></a>**8 an t-Iuchar, FE 403** — *A strand south of Baile chrom burned in the dark*. Boats out of no household raid a fishing strand half a day south of Baile chrom in the small hours of a moonless night, burning two houses to their footings and stripping the drying-racks bare. A woman of the strand says she knew two of the raiders by their voices, and will not name them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0050"><em>The outlaws of the north-west waters</em>, 26 an t-Sultain, FE 401</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4013"><em>Murchadh Ruadh's household loses its right</em>, 6 an Lùnastal, FE 398</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0051"></a>**28 an Lùnastal, FE 405** — *The boat lost off the north-west* (Uilebheist na Mara). A fishing boat out of Baile chrom is lost in calm water off the north-western coast. The two men who swim home say that something rose under it. Each year thereafter the boat's village keeps a wake for it. Of the thing they saw no more is told.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4015"></a>**9 an t-Ògmhios, FE 406** — *The wake first kept for the five* (Baile chrom). A year to the day after Cailean Buidhe's boat is lost in the calm off Baile chrom, the strand sets out a bowl for the five who went out on her and speaks the boat's name once over it. Anndra Cìobair, one of the two who swam home, pours the first cup, and goes on pouring it every year after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0051"><em>The boat lost off the north-west</em>, 28 an Lùnastal, FE 405</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4014"><em>A strand south of Baile chrom burned in the dark</em>, 8 an t-Iuchar, FE 403</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0052"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, FE 409** — *The fire at Baile chrom relit* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). After the loss the fishers of Baile chrom light the old beacon on the point again, fed with driftwood as the Law requires. From it comes Taigh-solais Baile chrom.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4016"></a>**11 an Cèitean, FE 410** — *The keeping of the beacon falls to the households in turn* (Baile chrom). Once the old beacon on the Baile chrom headland is relit, the carrying of driftwood to feed it becomes a charge the coast's households take up one season at a time, the way other coasts keep a granary door or a toll-stick.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0052"><em>The fire at Baile chrom relit</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, FE 409</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0053"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, FE 413** — *Seann Bhrenn resettled* (Seann Bhrenn). Fishers from the north side of the mountain settle the harbour of Seann Bhrenn on the northern coast and keep its old name, as the western settlers kept Seann Warr's. They find a stone quay under the silt and use it.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4017"></a>**12 an Giblean, FE 414** — *Word of the stone quay travels the coast* (Baile chrom). News of the worked stone quay found under the silt at Seann Bhrenn reaches Baile chrom by trader's boat, grown in the telling to a buried town in one mouth and shrunk to a single stone in another, neither telling closer to the truth than the other.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0053"><em>Seann Bhrenn resettled</em>, 25 an Dàmhair, FE 413</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0054"></a>**20 am Faoilleach, FE 417** — *The ancestor-cairn at Cathair naomh* (Cathair naomh). The people of Cathair naomh in the north raise a cairn for their dead on the hill above the town, and bring it a stone at every burial. It is the greatest ancestor-cairn in the north, and it grows still.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4018"></a>**14 am Màrt, FE 418** — *Word of the cairn at Cathair naomh travels the coast* (Baile chrom). Word reaches Baile chrom of the growing ancestor-cairn on the hill above Cathair naomh, carried a stone at a time at every burial, and travellers who see it years apart swear the hill itself looks changed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0054"><em>The ancestor-cairn at Cathair naomh</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, FE 417</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0055"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, FE 421** — *The panthers let pass* (Imrich nam Pantar). The crossing of the great cats is found to run straight over the carriers' southern road. Eilidh nic Ìomhair rules that no panther may be killed on the road in its season, and the carriers wait in the waypoint houses until the crossing is done. The rule is kept, for it costs the carriers only time.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4019"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, FE 421** — *The carriers of the southern road grumble at the panthers' ruling*. Told as far as Baile chrom, the tale of Eilidh nic Ìomhair's ruling on the great cats' crossing carries with it the carriers' first grumbling at the delay, and her answer that a Law which measures every handful can measure a few days' patience too.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0055"><em>The panthers let pass</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, FE 421</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4020"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, FE 430** — *The granaries of Dùn dhearg opened to households not its own* (Dùn dhearg). Sliochd Ìomhair opens the new granaries at Dùn dhearg to any household of the lowland plain caught short by the storm season, not only its own.
