Coinneach Mòr, still a young man of Seann Dunn, watches the queue at the gate and hears his father call it a debt of bread that few who take it yet feel as a debt.
- <a id="ev-II-0056"></a>**19 am Màrt, FE 434** — *The granaries of Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). Sliochd Ìomhair builds stone granaries at Dùn dhearg and fills them from the lowland fields of its share, holding grain against the storm season as the old custom of sharing asks. So the house gains what the Hall never had: people who owe it their bread.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4020"><em>The granaries of Dùn dhearg opened to households not its own</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, FE 430</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4021"></a>**7 am Faoilleach, FE 440** — *Anndra Cìobair dies at Baile chrom* (Baile chrom). Anndra Cìobair, who swam home from Cailean Buidhe's boat and kept the wake's first cup for near forty years, dies in his own bed above the strand he never left, and is buried within sight of the headland he tended.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0051"><em>The boat lost off the north-west</em>, 28 an Lùnastal, FE 405</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4022"></a>**12 an Dàmhair, FE 445** — *The resting-place at the foot of the pass becomes Baile Mòr dhomhain* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). The carriers' resting-place at the last flat ground before the high pass grows byres, a smithy and an inn that is never empty in the season the pass is open, and takes the name Baile Mòr dhomhain, though it stands on no deep water and lives by the pass and little else.
- <a id="ev-II-0057"></a>**18 an Gearran, FE 448** — *Baile Mòr dhomhain at the foot of the pass* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). Carriers who take the Hall's baskets north over the high pass settle at its southern foot, where Baile Mòr dhomhain now stands, to rest their beasts before the climb. The town lives by the pass, and by little else.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4022"><em>The resting-place at the foot of the pass becomes Baile Mòr dhomhain</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, FE 445</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0058"></a>**16 an Cèitean, FE 461** — *The reverent centuries*. Generation after generation mines the same small measure and burns the same small measure, and the people neither grow nor dwindle, whichever lord's share they live in. The rolls call them the reverent centuries.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4023"></a>**20 am Faoilleach, FE 475** — *Coinneach Mòr chosen Keeper of Sliochd Thormoid* (Seann Dunn). In the month of Giblean, the four houses choose Coinneach Mòr mac Tormoid, five-and-twenty, first Keeper of his house, for his patience rather than any gift of speech, judging a Keeper who keeps a flame steadily worth more than one who keeps it brilliantly for a short while.
- <a id="ev-II-0059"></a>**17 an Giblean, FE 475** — *Coinneach Mòr mac Tormoid keeps the flame* (Seann Dunn). Coinneach Mòr mac Tormoid of Seann Dunn becomes the first Keeper of Sliochd Thormoid. He keeps the flame longer than any Keeper before him, and changes nothing while he keeps it.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4023"><em>Coinneach Mòr chosen Keeper of Sliochd Thormoid</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, FE 475</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4024"></a>**4 an Giblean, FE 476** — *Griogair Ruadh asks a seat for Achadh chaol and is refused* (Achadh chaol). The headman of the shepherds at Achadh chaol asks the council at Dùn ìseal for a seat among the houses that govern the plain, and is refused for want of hearth-right cut in stone at the Roinn. He sits one courtesy season and goes home with the dues still owed and no seat won.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4023"><em>Coinneach Mòr chosen Keeper of Sliochd Thormoid</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, FE 475</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0060"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, FE 488** — *The shepherds of Achadh chaol* (Achadh chaol). Shepherds settle the upland fields at Achadh chaol in the north-east and send their wool down to the harbours. Their headman sits one season on the council at Dùn ìseal, is found to hold no hearth-right, and goes home.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4024"><em>Griogair Ruadh asks a seat for Achadh chaol and is refused</em>, 4 an Giblean, FE 476</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4025"></a>**3 an Cèitean, FE 490** — *Coinneach's walkers set out to list the ruins*. Coinneach Mòr sends six walkers the length of the plain to list every ruin standing on ground the four houses claim, ruling before they leave that the list shall say only who does not own each place, and never guess who built it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4024"><em>Griogair Ruadh asks a seat for Achadh chaol and is refused</em>, 4 an Giblean, FE 476</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4026"></a>**5 an Gearran, FE 492** — *The walkers return with the list of the old people's ruins* (Làrach an Dùin-fhaire). The walkers come home after two years with Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, Làrach an Dùin, Làrach an Teampaill and the plain's scattered standing stones set down on one list, each entry naming who does not hold the ground and none guessing at the builders, who are called after only the old people.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4025"><em>Coinneach's walkers set out to list the ruins</em>, 3 an Cèitean, FE 490</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4027"></a>**6 am Màrt, FE 498** — *The first ring of stakes raised round Carragh Cnoc bheag* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). Once the walkers' list names the standing stone above Cnoc bheag, the household nearest it fences the rise to keep cattle from rubbing the cut letters smooth. Each generation after renews the stakes, and the stone itself is never moved.
- <a id="ev-II-0061"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, FE 502** — *The Keepers' count of the old places* (Làrach an Dùin-fhaire). Coinneach Mòr sends walkers to list the ruins of the old people. They bring back Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, Làrach an Dùin, Làrach an Teampaill and the standing stones. The list says who does not own each place, and not who built it; the Keepers rule that it shall not guess.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4025"><em>Coinneach's walkers set out to list the ruins</em>, 3 an Cèitean, FE 490</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-4026"><em>The walkers return with the list of the old people's ruins</em>, 5 an Gearran, FE 492</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4028"></a>**29 an t-Iuchar, FE 505** — *The bath-house roofed over the springs of Muileann ruadh* (Muileann ruadh). After a cousin of his own house is carried to the warm springs half dead of a wasting cough and comes home breathing, Coinneach Mòr orders a bath-house raised over the largest pool, with sleeping-places for the sick and benches for those who wait out the cure beside them.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4029"></a>**27 an Lùnastal, FE 505** — *A keeper of the springs named in Dian Cècht's name* (Muileann ruadh). Coinneach Mòr names a widow who nursed her own husband through a wasting fever as keeper of the springs at Muileann ruadh, the office set in the healer Dian Cècht's name and answering to no measure of coal, the first such office the flame at Seann Dunn has made.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4028"><em>The bath-house roofed over the springs of Muileann ruadh</em>, 29 an t-Iuchar, FE 505</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4030"></a>**1 an t-Ògmhios, FE 508** — *The silversmiths of Muileann chiar cast their weights* (Muileann chiar). Weary of disputes at their own market, the silversmiths of Muileann chiar cast a set of weights from a barley-corn to a newborn lamb, checked one against another and set out for any trader to use. Within years a thing weighed there is called, the length of the carriers' roads, weighed fairly.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4031"></a>**3 an Cèitean, FE 513** — *Torcall Donn weds Muireall nic Ìomhair* (Dùn dhearg). Torcall Donn, great-grandson of Eithne nic Ailein and five-and-eighty, weds Muireall nic Ìomhair, not yet four-and-twenty, at Dùn dhearg, a match both houses call costless and both houses are pleased with, her marriage-portion drawn to satisfy both grants at once.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4032"></a>**29 an t-Iuchar, FE 514** — *Muireall nic Ìomhair dies in her first winter*. Muireall nic Ìomhair dies of a nine-day fever in her first winter as a wife, leaving no child and no settled answer to which grant, the house of Ìomhar's or the line of Eithne's, should hold her lands should she die too soon, since no one had thought she would.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4031"><em>Torcall Donn weds Muireall nic Ìomhair</em>, 3 an Cèitean, FE 513</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0062"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, FE 515** — *The fence round Carragh Cnoc bheag* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). The people of Cnoc bheag set a ring of stakes round the old standing stone above their town, that the cattle may not rub against it. Every generation after renews the ring. The stone is never moved.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4027"><em>The first ring of stakes raised round Carragh Cnoc bheag</em>, 6 am Màrt, FE 498</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4033"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, FE 515** — *Both houses claim Muireall's lands*. The house of Ìomhar claims Muireall's marriage-lands as returning to the kin that granted them; the line of Eithne claims the same ground as passing to the husband's holding. Both claims are argued with equal heat by men who never asked, while she lived, which grant should prevail.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4032"><em>Muireall nic Ìomhair dies in her first winter</em>, 29 an t-Iuchar, FE 514</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4034"></a>**5 an Gearran, FE 517** — *The first double-sworn field burned*. A holding sworn to both Dùn dhearg and Cathair mhòr since Muireall's marriage-portion touched it is burned in a single night by its own near neighbours, byre first and standing barley after. The household goes to kin elsewhere, and the ground lies unsown, claimed loudly and worked by neither house.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4033"><em>Both houses claim Muireall's lands</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, FE 515</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0063"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, FE 529** — *The bath-house at Muileann ruadh* (Muileann ruadh). A roofed bath-house is built over the warm springs below Muileann ruadh, with sleeping-places for the sick and their bearers. The Hall appoints a keeper of the springs, who tends them in the name of Dian Cècht, the healer. It is the first office the Hall makes that has nothing to do with the coal.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4028"><em>The bath-house roofed over the springs of Muileann ruadh</em>, 29 an t-Iuchar, FE 505</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-4029"><em>A keeper of the springs named in Dian Cècht's name</em>, 27 an Lùnastal, FE 505</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4035"></a>**7 am Faoilleach, FE 537** — *Coinneach Mòr dies at Seann Dunn* (Seann Dunn). Coinneach Mòr mac Tormoid dies at Seann Dunn in his eighty-seventh year, two-and-sixty years into his keeping, asking after the walkers' list and the burned marriage-lands in his last days, and leaving the flame to a nephew chosen in his stead with the smoke of the burnings still on the southern horizon.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0059"><em>Coinneach Mòr mac Tormoid keeps the flame</em>, 17 an Giblean, FE 475</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0064"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, FE 542** — *The silver weights of Muileann chiar* (Muileann chiar). The silversmiths of Muileann chiar cast a set of weights, the least the weight of a barley-corn and the greatest that of a newborn lamb. Every trader on the carriers' roads comes to use them, and for the rest of the age a thing weighed at Muileann chiar is said to be weighed fairly.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4030"><em>The silversmiths of Muileann chiar cast their weights</em>, 1 an t-Ògmhios, FE 508</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4036"></a>**4 an Giblean, FE 543** — *Fearghas sends the last untroubled tithe* (Achadh mhòr). Fearghas Dà-Mhionn weighs out his sheaves for Dùn dhearg and for Cathair mhòr at Muileann chiar as he has every harvest of his long life, a little short to each, not yet knowing it is the last year either hall will let the joke stand.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4037"></a>**6 am Màrt, FE 544** — *The black-eaved holding east of Achadh mhòr*. A double-sworn household two valleys east chooses the Red Share and is burned to its field-walls by Cathair mhòr's men before the next harvest, its cattle driven off and its house left standing empty as a warning to the next household asked to choose.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4038"></a>**19 am Faoilleach, FE 545** — *A holding that chose neither is burned by both*. A double-sworn holding south of Achadh mhòr refuses to choose between its lords and is burned within the year by both hosts in turn, the Red Share's riders taking the barn first and a company of Cathair mhòr's finishing it, each telling its own men it punished only what the other began.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4039"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, FE 546** — *Fearghas rides to see a burned holding*. Fearghas rides to the black-eaved holding east of his own fields to see with his own eyes what a double-sworn household looks like once burned, and finds only standing walls, fallen roofs and a dog that will not leave the ruin, and speaks of the war differently after.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4040"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, FE 547** — *A burned widow's household shelters at Achadh mhòr* (Achadh mhòr). A widow and her three sons, burned out in the southern raids, shelter three nights at Fearghas's hall on their way to kin beyond Ceann leathan, and Fearghas feeds them without asking any oath of them, telling his steward a household already burned has paid enough.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4039"><em>Fearghas rides to see a burned holding</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, FE 546</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4041"></a>**18 am Faoilleach, FE 548** — *Torcall Donn killed on the road below Dùn thais*. Torcall Donn, great-grandson of Eithne and husband of the dead Muireall nic Ìomhair, is killed at a hundred and eighteen years old when his company meets a company of the Red Share's riders on a narrow road and the pushing between them turns to blows.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4042"></a>**16 an Gearran, FE 548** — *Fearghas sends barley to be burned at Torcall Donn's grave* (Cathair mhòr). Fearghas sends a measure of his own barley to be burned at Torcall Donn's graveside at Cathair mhòr, the old rite for a man dead before his harvest is in, asking that no word go with it saying who sent it; the giver is known within the season regardless.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4041"><em>Torcall Donn killed on the road below Dùn thais</em>, 18 am Faoilleach, FE 548</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4043"></a>**17 am Màrt, FE 549** — *The Red Share presses its claim after the widower's death* (Dùn dhearg). With Torcall Donn dead, the Red Share presses its claim on Muireall's three granges harder rather than less, judging Cathair mhòr's grip on lands held only through a dead man's marriage weaker than before, and the war burns on past the quarrel that began it.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4044"></a>**15 an Giblean, FE 550** — *Ciorstaidh's stone set in Fearghas's hall* (Achadh mhòr). Fearghas has a stone cut for his grandmother Ciorstaidh and set into his own hall wall, her name and the sign of the cut knot beside it, wanting it known in stone that the house he holds was held first by one of the eleven who answered for their double oath all their lives.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4045"></a>**14 an Cèitean, FE 550** — *The mason of Muileann chiar carries the tale*. The stone-cutter who set Ciorstaidh's memorial breaks his promise of silence at the first market he reaches, and the setting of the stone becomes, within a season, one more thing told of Fearghas Dà-Mhionn on both sides of the war, read two different ways by two different hearths.
- <a id="ev-II-0064b"></a>**24 an Lùnastal, FE 556** — *The burning of Achadh mhòr* (Achadh mhòr). Cogadh an Dà Mhionn, the War of the Two Oaths, ends where it began. Fearghas Dà-Mhionn, lord of the granary fields of Achadh mhòr, sworn both to the line of Ìomhar and to the lords of Cathair mhòr, is called to arms by each against the other, and both come to take his fields. The fields are burned to the stubble, and Fearghas dies in his hall.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4031"><em>Torcall Donn weds Muireall nic Ìomhair</em>, 3 an Cèitean, FE 513</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4032"><em>Muireall nic Ìomhair dies in her first winter</em>, 29 an t-Iuchar, FE 514</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4033"><em>Both houses claim Muireall's lands</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, FE 515</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4034"><em>The first double-sworn field burned</em>, 5 an Gearran, FE 517</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4036"><em>Fearghas sends the last untroubled tithe</em>, 4 an Giblean, FE 543</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4037"><em>The black-eaved holding east of Achadh mhòr</em>, 6 am Màrt, FE 544</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4038"><em>A holding that chose neither is burned by both</em>, 19 am Faoilleach, FE 545</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4039"><em>Fearghas rides to see a burned holding</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, FE 546</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4040"><em>A burned widow's household shelters at Achadh mhòr</em>, 20 an Dùbhlachd, FE 547</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4041"><em>Torcall Donn killed on the road below Dùn thais</em>, 18 am Faoilleach, FE 548</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-4042"><em>Fearghas sends barley to be burned at Torcall Donn's grave</em>, 16 an Gearran, FE 548</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-4043"><em>The Red Share presses its claim after the widower's death</em>, 17 am Màrt, FE 549</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-4044"><em>Ciorstaidh's stone set in Fearghas's hall</em>, 15 an Giblean, FE 550</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-4045"><em>The mason of Muileann chiar carries the tale</em>, 14 an Cèitean, FE 550</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0064c"></a>**1 an t-Samhain, FE 556** — *Sìth an Stairsnich* (Dùn ìseal). The lords of the shares swear the Peace of the Threshold, Sìth an Stairsnich, on the threshold of Talla na Lasrach, beside the stone cup, with the Keeper as witness. No share may be parted again at a death: a holding passes whole to one heir. No man may swear to two lords. The boundary stones are set where they stand that day. So ends Aimhreit nan Oighrean.
- <a id="ev-II-0064a"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556** — *The market under the Hall* (Dùn ìseal). A market is held under the walls of the Hall at Dùn ìseal on the four quarter days, Samhain, Là Fhèill Brìde, Bealltainn and Lùnastal, when the households of the eastern hills come up with their dues. Hides, venison, charcoal, honey and the silver of Muileann chiar change hands there on the new weights. The Keepers allow no coal to be sold on their ground, and none is.
- <a id="ev-EIII-4046"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556** — *Both hosts called out for Achadh mhòr* (Achadh mhòr). In the heat of Lùnastal the Red Share's council and Cathair mhòr's both resolve within the same week to take Achadh mhòr's granary whole, and two riders reach Fearghas within an hour of each other, each astonished that his own lord's host was not first to move.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0064b"><em>The burning of Achadh mhòr</em>, 24 an Lùnastal, FE 556</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4047"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556** — *The last sheaf of Achadh mhòr carried clear of the fire* (Achadh mhòr). The reapers finish the western cutting and carry the last sheaf, bound and cut high as the custom asks, clear of the burning fields before the wind turns, and it is this sheaf, not the granary, that the households round about keep afterward at every harvest's end.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-II-0064b"><em>The burning of Achadh mhòr</em>, 24 an Lùnastal, FE 556</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4048"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556** — *The waypoint house at Muileann chiar begins tallying grain* (Muileann chiar). In the season after Achadh mhòr's burning, the keeper of the waypoint house on the road below Muileann chiar chalks a slate with every granary along the carriers' road still holding grain, and rubs it out and chalks it again as the hungry winter empties one store after another. Carriers come to ask him for news of bread before they ask for news of the war.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0064b"><em>The burning of Achadh mhòr</em>, 24 an Lùnastal, FE 556</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4049"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556** — *A household of the middle plain sends its youngest son begging seed corn*. A family two days' walk from Achadh mhòr's blackened fields sends its youngest son round every kinsman it has, sworn or unsworn to either share, asking only for seed corn against the spring sowing and not for grain to eat that winter. He comes home with less than he asked for, gathered a handful at a time from households as pinched as his own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0064b"><em>The burning of Achadh mhòr</em>, 24 an Lùnastal, FE 556</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4050"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556** — *Ruairidh Glas writes to Eithne nic Ailein* (Dùn dhearg). Ruairidh Glas, holder of the Red Share at Dùn dhearg, sends word to Eithne nic Ailein of Cathair mhòr's plain that a war fought over a granary which no longer stands profits neither of their hungry households, and asks her to name ground where neither hall need be ashamed to meet.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0064c"><em>Sìth an Stairsnich</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 556</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4051"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556** — *Eithne nic Ailein names the threshold of Talla na Lasrach* (Dùn ìseal). Eithne nic Ailein answers Ruairidh Glas that she will set foot in no hall of the Red Share's, as he will set foot in none of hers, and names instead the threshold of Talla na Lasrach at Dùn ìseal, where the stone cup stands on ground that belongs to no share and never has.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0064c"><em>Sìth an Stairsnich</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 556</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4050"><em>Ruairidh Glas writes to Eithne nic Ailein</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4052"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556** — *A reluctant lord is shamed into the swearing*. The steward of a lesser holding north of Achadh mhòr answers Eithne's summons that his lord sees no profit in standing bareheaded before an old woman to be told what he knows already. Eithne sends back that he may explain to his own hungry households why the peace that feeds everyone else's has passed his door by, and he comes a season late to swear it.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0064c"><em>Sìth an Stairsnich</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 556</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4051"><em>Eithne nic Ailein names the threshold of Talla na Lasrach</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4053"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556** — *Eithne nic Ailein is carried up to Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). Eithne nic Ailein, whose legs have long since stopped carrying her, is borne up the old carriers' road to Dùn ìseal in a chair, one pole carried by Niall Òg, who has outlived nearly every other soul that remembers the valley of the Roinn, and who tells her, on the road, that she is the last one left who remembers what he remembers.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0064c"><em>Sìth an Stairsnich</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 556</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-4052"><em>A reluctant lord is shamed into the swearing</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4054"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556** — *The Keeper drafts and reads the terms of the Threshold* (Dùn ìseal). At the asking of both halls, neither of which trusts the other's clerks to write the terms fairly, the Keeper of the flame drafts the peace herself and reads it aloud to the gathered stones before any lord is asked to swear, so that the households standing beyond the lords may carry the whole of it home in their own words.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0064c"><em>Sìth an Stairsnich</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 556</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4055"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556** — *Ruairidh Glas speaks of the first blood at Dùn thais* (Dùn ìseal). Swearing the Peace of the Threshold with his hand still on the stone cup, Ruairidh Glas says before the gathered lords that he shed the first blood of the strife at Dùn thais over cattle on a wet slope, when he was young enough to think a stone worth a life, and that he would not buy it again for twice the grazing on the island.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0001c"><em>First blood among the heirs</em>, 17 an Giblean, FE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4056"></a>**30 am Faoilleach, FE 557** — *A double-sworn household on the old boundary gives up one oath* (Achadh mhòr). A household sworn to two lords since a marriage two generations back keeps the oath that has cost it least and lets the other lapse before the spring sowing, its eldest son reasoning aloud that neither hall's carrier had once knocked on their door in the whole of the hungry winter past.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0064c"><em>Sìth an Stairsnich</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 556</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4057"></a>**11 an t-Iuchar, FE 557** — *The first Threshold market stands thin and unparted* (Dùn ìseal). The first quarter-day market held below Talla na Lasrach after the Peace draws little to sell, the hungry winter having left small surplus, and many households come only to watch whether a trader of the Red Share can stand at a stall beside one of Cathair mhòr's plain without a steward of either hall coming to part them. None comes.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0064a"><em>The market under the Hall</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, FE 556</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-4058"></a>**9 an Lùnastal, FE 557** — *The boundary lines of the middle plain settle by the sowing*. By the time of the spring sowing after the Peace, the boundary lines that had shifted and blurred through forty years of burning have settled again into a shape that will hold for longer than any lord who swore to it that Samhain will live to see, with only small mendings asked at Dùn ìseal in the years after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0064c"><em>Sìth an Stairsnich</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 556</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0065"></a>**28 am Faoilleach, FE 565** — *The stag's people at Cnoc bhàn* (Cnoc bhàn). A house of the stag's people is founded at Cnoc bhàn, north of the mountain, and after the long exclusion takes cutters again. Its teachers keep the question of Sìleas nic Coinnich as she left it: why does the coal show its colours for one hand and not another?
- <a id="ev-EIII-5001"></a>**2 an t-Sultain, FE 571** — *The nine hearths raise Seonaid Chiar to the flame* (Dùn ìseal). The nine hearths of Dùn ìseal raise Seonaid Chiar of the house of Muireach to the flame at six-and-twenty years old, the youngest Keeper chosen since Muireach Liath's own day. Her grandmother, a cutter of the galleries all her working life, warns her that a young Keeper who bends once in her first year is asked to bend again for the rest of her keeping.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5002"></a>**4 an Lùnastal, FE 573** — *Three teachers of Cnoc bhàn set an unlit lamp before the Hall's door* (Dùn ìseal). Three old teachers of the stag's school at Cnoc bhàn climb the mountain road on foot and set an unlit lamp on the stones before Talla na Lasrach, asking only to be let back among the cutters already working the galleries, and swearing to ask nothing of the vein aloud if the Hall will stop asking whether they have any right to stand near it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5001"><em>The nine hearths raise Seonaid Chiar to the flame</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, FE 571</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0066"></a>**26 an Gearran, FE 574** — *Seonaid Chiar reopens the galleries to the stag's people* (Dùn ìseal). Seonaid Chiar, Keeper of the house of Muireach, lets cutters trained by the stag's people back into the galleries at Dùn ìseal, sworn to ask nothing of the vein aloud. The Hall's roll calls it a reconciling. The school remembers it as a truce.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5001"><em>The nine hearths raise Seonaid Chiar to the flame</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, FE 571</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5002"><em>Three teachers of Cnoc bhàn set an unlit lamp before the Hall's door</em>, 4 an Lùnastal, FE 573</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0067"></a>**27 am Màrt, FE 579** — *Cathair mhòr walled* (Cathair mhòr). The people of Cathair mhòr on the southern coast build a wall of fitted stone about their headland town, the first town wall on the island. What they feared no one has told.
- <a id="ev-II-0068"></a>**16 am Faoilleach, FE 584** — *Ceann leathan's fish-market* (Ceann leathan). Ceann leathan becomes the market of the southern fishing and sends dried fish inland along the carriers' paths. Its harbour-master keeps tallies on notched sticks. Several are kept at Muileann chaol, the oldest counted things in its keeping.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5003"></a>**6 an t-Iuchar, FE 585** — *Seonaid Chiar's guild judgment at Cnoc leathan* (Dùn ìseal). Hearing two carriers of Cnoc leathan's guild each accuse the other of taking a fee out of turn, Seonaid Chiar asks only which of them had first offered to give the disputed load back, and, hearing neither had, tells them the Hall's grant is a right to carry and not a right to quarrel. The two settle the matter themselves before they have gone a mile down the mountain road.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5002"><em>Three teachers of Cnoc bhàn set an unlit lamp before the Hall's door</em>, 4 an Lùnastal, FE 573</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0069"></a>**14 an Gearran, FE 589** — *The shrine at Inis thais* (Inis thais). A shrine to the ancestors lost at sea is raised at Inis thais on the western coast. Its keepers burn their season's handful on the shore and not indoors, so that the drowned, gone west over the sea, may see it.
- <a id="ev-II-0070"></a>**29 an Giblean, FE 594** — *Cuan shean's salt-pans* (Cuan shean). The people of Cuan shean on the western coast dig salt-pans on the flats below the town and boil sea-water over peat. Their salt goes inland along the western road and keeps the fish of half the island.
- <a id="ev-II-0071"></a>**31 am Màrt, FE 599** — *Salt-carriers on the heath above Baile fhiadhaich* (Baile fhiadhaich). Salt-carriers from Cuan shean settle on the western heath above Baile fhiadhaich, by a stream that runs all summer. The heath about it is not worth the plough, and its people keep goats.

## The Years FE 601 – 800

- <a id="ev-II-0072"></a>**2 am Màrt, FE 604** — *The sunny house* (An Taigh-òsta Grianach). A waypoint house is built on the eastern road where the carriers from Cnoc leathan meet the southern coast path, on the site of An Taigh-òsta Grianach. It faces south, and from the first is known for its warmth, which is all its name has ever meant.
- <a id="ev-II-0073"></a>**1 an Gearran, FE 609** — *Cnoc leathan's market* (Cnoc leathan). Cnoc leathan, at the eastern end of the road past the sunny house, becomes the market town of the south-eastern hills. Its carriers' guild holds the right to carry for the Hall on the stretch down to the coast.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-5003"><em>Seonaid Chiar's guild judgment at Cnoc leathan</em>, 6 an t-Iuchar, FE 585</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5004"></a>**7 an t-Ògmhios, FE 611** — *Ruairidh Glas stands once more before the stone cup* (Dùn ìseal). In his nine hundred and ninth year, Ruairidh Glas, holder of the Red Share, asks unasked leave to climb Dùn ìseal on foot and stand again before the stone cup, though no lord of a share is required to outside the quarter days. He says nothing aloud that any living ear catches, and goes back down the same evening to Dùn dhearg.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0064c"><em>Sìth an Stairsnich</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 556</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5003"><em>Seonaid Chiar's guild judgment at Cnoc leathan</em>, 6 an t-Iuchar, FE 585</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5005"></a>**10 an Giblean, FE 612** — *Ruairidh Glas dies at Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). Ruairidh Glas dies in his own bed at Dùn dhearg, having lived nine hundred and ten years and never once returned to Dùn thais since the morning he shed the first blood of the strife of the heirs there. He outlives every soul who stood beside him at the ford where his grandfather's line first took the Red Hill.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0001c"><em>First blood among the heirs</em>, 17 an Giblean, FE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5004"><em>Ruairidh Glas stands once more before the stone cup</em>, 7 an t-Ògmhios, FE 611</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5006"></a>**9 an Cèitean, FE 612** — *The Red Share passes without a summons to the Hall* (Dùn dhearg). Ruairidh Glas's son takes up the Red Share at Dùn dhearg without any summons to the Hall, as the Peace of the Threshold requires none where an heir is named and undisputed. The season's rolls, careful to name every lesser lord, stay strangely thin about naming this one, a silence the Hall's clerk lays to the household's own quiet rather than to any failure of the pen.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0064c"><em>Sìth an Stairsnich</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, FE 556</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5005"><em>Ruairidh Glas dies at Dùn dhearg</em>, 10 an Giblean, FE 612</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0074"></a>**23 an Lùnastal, FE 614** — *The fall in the high gallery* (Dùn ìseal). A roof falls in the highest gallery at Dùn ìseal and kills four cutters. The gallery is walled up and left. Seonaid Chiar orders props of oak set in every gallery after, and for the first time the Hall spends timber on the mountain.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5007"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, FE 614** — *The four dead of the high gallery are buried on the Hall's own ground* (Dùn ìseal). The four cutters killed when the roof of the highest gallery falls at Dùn ìseal are carried up and buried on the Hall's own ground, the one ground on the island no feud has ever been let to follow a man. Seonaid Chiar sets the last stone over the last of them with her own hands, which no Keeper before her is remembered to have done.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0074"><em>The fall in the high gallery</em>, 23 an Lùnastal, FE 614</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5008"></a>**21 an Cèitean, FE 615** — *The first oak props are cut for the galleries* (Dùn ìseal). After a season's argument over how a gallery roof should ever be held against another such fall, Seonaid Chiar orders timber props of oak set in every gallery the Hall works, the first timber the Hall has ever spent on the mountain itself. The first oak is felled and cut within the season, so that no gallery stands unpropped by the following year's cutting.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0074"><em>The fall in the high gallery</em>, 23 an Lùnastal, FE 614</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5007"><em>The four dead of the high gallery are buried on the Hall's own ground</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, FE 614</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5009"></a>**10 an Giblean, FE 630** — *Seonaid Chiar dies above the galleries she kept* (Dùn ìseal). Seonaid Chiar dies in her own quarters above the galleries at Dùn ìseal, eighty-five years old, having held the flame the better part of six decades. The nine hearths that raised her young choose another after her without any dispute the rolls think worth setting down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0066"><em>Seonaid Chiar reopens the galleries to the stag's people</em>, 26 an Gearran, FE 574</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5008"><em>The first oak props are cut for the galleries</em>, 21 an Cèitean, FE 615</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5010"></a>**22 an Giblean, FE 630** — *The school at Cnoc bhàn returns its unlit lamp* (Dùn ìseal). On word of Seonaid Chiar's death, the school at Cnoc bhàn sends no delegation and no message of grief, only the same unlit lamp its three old teachers once set before her door, carried back up by cutters young enough to have known no other Keeper, and left again on the same stones, still unlit.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0066"><em>Seonaid Chiar reopens the galleries to the stag's people</em>, 26 an Gearran, FE 574</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5009"><em>Seonaid Chiar dies above the galleries she kept</em>, 10 an Giblean, FE 630</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0075"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, FE 634** — *Cathair dhomhain founded* (Cathair dhomhain). Carriers settled at the mouth of the western road raise a town on the rise above the harbour and name it Cathair dhomhain. Its shrine keeps the Law's measure strictly, and its people are proud of it.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5011"></a>**9 an Cèitean, FE 635** — *Cathair dhomhain's shrine holds the Law to the grain* (Cathair dhomhain). The new shrine at Cathair dhomhain keeps the Small-Burning Law to the very grain from its founding day, a strictness the town becomes known for beyond any other pride it holds. Lowland households speak of it for a lifetime, though the town itself remains a place carriers pass through on the way to somewhere else.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0075"><em>Cathair dhomhain founded</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, FE 634</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0076"></a>**26 an t-Ògmhios, FE 654** — *A fishing town at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). The old settlement of the Red Hill, shrunk to a small fishing town, grows again at the western bridge-foot on the Abhainn dhomhain, a little above its meeting with the Abhainn gheal below Loch chrom. The ground is afterwards called Cathair dhearg, for its red stone. As yet it is a place carriers pass through on the way to somewhere else.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5012"></a>**7 an t-Ògmhios, FE 660** — *The death of Cailean* (Dùn dhearg). Cailean, a cousin of Goraidh mac Ìomhair through their grandmothers, dies under a wall he is mending at his own hall in a night of high wind. He leaves no child of his body, and his county of the east goes unclaimed.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5013"></a>**6 an t-Iuchar, FE 662** — *The death of Donnchadh* (Dùn dhearg). Donnchadh, Cailean's younger brother, dies of a cough the hearth-women cannot cut, with his sister's hand in his. He too leaves no child, and the second of the three old counties east of Dùn dhearg is left without an heir named.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5012"><em>The death of Cailean</em>, 7 an t-Ògmhios, FE 660</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5014"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, FE 668** — *Goraidh's marriage to Muirne nic Dhonnchaidh* (Dùn dhearg). Goraidh mac Ìomhair rides to Muirne nic Dhonnchaidh, a widowed kinswoman of four hundred years who holds the third of the old eastern counties alone, and marries her in the spring. Her county comes whole into the marriage, as the Peace of the Threshold allows, and Goraidh takes on her dead husbands' debts to the county's smiths.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5013"><em>The death of Donnchadh</em>, 6 an t-Iuchar, FE 662</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5015"></a>**13 am Faoilleach, FE 669** — *Goraidh rides the three counties* (Dùn dhearg). Through the first year of the marriage Goraidh mac Ìomhair walks the boundaries of all three gathered counties with Muirne beside him, eating at the hearths and not the halls, learning which streams have moved and which grazings are old enough to fight over.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5014"><em>Goraidh's marriage to Muirne nic Dhonnchaidh</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, FE 668</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5016"></a>**11 an Gearran, FE 672** — *The hungry harvests* (Dùn dhearg). Two summers running the rains come at the wrong end of the season and the barley rots standing in the low ground east of Dùn dhearg. Goraidh mac Ìomhair opens all four of his granaries and gives grain outright to nine households that cannot pay even the lowered price.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5015"><em>Goraidh rides the three counties</em>, 13 am Faoilleach, FE 669</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0076a"></a>**3 an Giblean, FE 674** — *Goraidh gathers the shares of the east* (Dùn dhearg). By two cousins dead without heirs and a marriage to a third, Goraidh mac Ìomhair holds in one hand three of the old counties of the east round Dùn dhearg, parted since the Roinn. He is the first of the kin to gather again what the Roinn had divided, and the Peace of the Threshold lets him keep it whole.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5012"><em>The death of Cailean</em>, 7 an t-Ògmhios, FE 660</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5013"><em>The death of Donnchadh</em>, 6 an t-Iuchar, FE 662</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-5014"><em>Goraidh's marriage to Muirne nic Dhonnchaidh</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, FE 668</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-5015"><em>Goraidh rides the three counties</em>, 13 am Faoilleach, FE 669</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0077"></a>**28 an Cèitean, FE 674** — *Goraidh mac Ìomhair called rìgh* (Dùn dhearg). At Dùn dhearg the lowland households who eat from the granaries of Sliochd Ìomhair begin to call its head, Goraidh mac Ìomhair, their rìgh, their king. No one had been so called since Ailean Mòr, for at the Roinn the heirs swore that none of them would take the word. Goraidh claims nothing over the vein, and is careful to tell the Hall so.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5016"><em>The hungry harvests</em>, 11 an Gearran, FE 672</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5017"></a>**12 am Màrt, FE 677** — *Death of Muirne nic Dhonnchaidh* (Dùn dhearg). Muirne nic Dhonnchaidh dies in her sleep in the ninth year of her marriage to Goraidh mac Ìomhair, with her own county's reciter in the room. He buries her among her own dead, as she asked him.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0076a"><em>Goraidh gathers the shares of the east</em>, 3 an Giblean, FE 674</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5016"><em>The hungry harvests</em>, 11 an Gearran, FE 672</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5018"></a>**28 an t-Samhain, FE 688** — *The timber hall of Dùn dhearg raised with a granary at each corner* (Dùn dhearg). Goraidh mac Ìomhair raises a long hall of squared oak on his father's rise at Dùn dhearg, with a granary at each of its four corners. The carpenters of the Red Share and of the three gathered counties raise it side by side, and the granaries are filled from all four counties in one season.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5017"><em>Death of Muirne nic Dhonnchaidh</em>, 12 am Màrt, FE 677</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5019"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, FE 693** — *Goraidh leaves his spear at the last house* (Dùn ìseal). Come to answer the council's word, Goraidh mac Ìomhair leaves his spear with his men at the last waypoint house on the mountain road and climbs to Dùn ìseal on foot and unarmed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5018"><em>The timber hall of Dùn dhearg raised with a granary at each corner</em>, 28 an t-Samhain, FE 688</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0078"></a>**9 an t-Sultain, FE 694** — *The division of keeping* (Dùn ìseal). The council at Dùn ìseal and Goraidh mac Ìomhair agree on a division. The Keeper keeps the flame and the galleries; the rìgh keeps the roads, the granaries and the peace of the lowlands. The rìgh may not enter the galleries, and the Keeper may not raise spears. On this division the island is governed for the rest of the age.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5019"><em>Goraidh leaves his spear at the last house</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, FE 693</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5020"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, FE 694** — *The waypoint-keepers gather the road toll for a share* (Dùn dhearg). Goraidh does not gather the toll of one fish in twenty himself. He gives it to the keepers of the waypoint houses along each road, who have kept a bed and a fire for carriers since before his grandfather's day, and lets each keep a share of what they take.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5019"><em>Goraidh leaves his spear at the last house</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, FE 693</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5021"></a>**16 an Lùnastal, FE 703** — *A waypoint-keeper's short tally forgiven*. At a waypoint house on the northern road a keeper's first season's toll comes in a tenth short, for want of anyone at the door by night. Goraidh mac Ìomhair laughs at the reckoning and lets the shortfall stand.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5020"><em>The waypoint-keepers gather the road toll for a share</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, FE 694</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0079"></a>**11 an Lùnastal, FE 714** — *Goraidh Mòr's hall* (Dùn dhearg). Goraidh mac Ìomhair, called Goraidh Mòr, builds a timber hall on the hill at Dùn dhearg, with a granary at each corner. Its post-holes could still be seen when the surveyors of the Library walked the hill, and they measured and drew them.
- <a id="ev-II-0080"></a>**22 an t-Sultain, FE 719** — *The first road-toll* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). Goraidh Mòr sets a toll on the carriers' roads, one fish in twenty or its worth, to pay the road-guards and keep up the bridges. The keepers of the waypoint houses gather it, and keep a share of it, and the rolls say so.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-5021"><em>A waypoint-keeper's short tally forgiven</em>, 16 an Lùnastal, FE 703</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5022"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, FE 725** — *Mòrag takes up the walking of the roads* (Dùn dhearg). Goraidh's daughter Mòrag, who could never sit still in a hall, takes over the walking of the island's roads from her ageing father long before he will call it a handing-over. He lets her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5021"><em>A waypoint-keeper's short tally forgiven</em>, 16 an Lùnastal, FE 703</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5023"></a>**13 an Dàmhair, FE 736** — *Dòmhnall's fall from the cart* (Dùn dhearg). Dòmhnall, riding the back board of a laden cart above the ford, is thrown under its wheel where it strikes a stone left standing proud of the road-bed. His leg is set and set again and never knits true; he walks with a stick the rest of his life.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5024"></a>**22 an Giblean, FE 753** — *Death of Goraidh Mòr* (Dùn dhearg). Goraidh mac Ìomhair dies in his own hall at Dùn dhearg in his two hundred and thirteenth year, in the granary month, asking after the notching of the western road's toll-sticks. His daughter Mòrag and two waypoint-keepers rendering their tallies are with him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5022"><em>Mòrag takes up the walking of the roads</em>, 11 an t-Samhain, FE 725</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5025"></a>**21 an Cèitean, FE 753** — *The toll-stick notched at Mòr nic Dhùghaill's old house* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). Days after Goraidh Mòr's death, the keeper of the old waypoint house that was Mòr nic Dhùghaill's notches a fresh toll-stick for a carrier's fish and a carrier's wool, as she has every week before and will every week after, whoever holds the hall at Dùn dhearg.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0080"><em>The first road-toll</em>, 22 an t-Sultain, FE 719</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0081"></a>**21 an Dàmhair, FE 754** — *Mòrag of the Roads* (Dùn dhearg). Mòrag nic Ghoraidh takes the hall at Dùn dhearg after her father Goraidh Mòr. She is called Mòrag nan Rathad, Mòrag of the Roads, for in her first years she walks every carriers' road on the island and orders the bad stretches made anew.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5024"><em>Death of Goraidh Mòr</em>, 22 an Giblean, FE 753</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5026"></a>**18 an t-Iuchar, FE 756** — *The toll-chest counted at a keeper's own door* (Dùn dhearg). Mòrag nan Rathad finds the toll-house two days east of the ford unanswered longest of all its keepers' letters. She has her road-guards open the keeper's own chest and counts the silver on a cloth before him, takes half for the mending, and leaves half for his household.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0081"><em>Mòrag of the Roads</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, FE 754</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5027"></a>**25 am Faoilleach, FE 760** — *Mòrag meets Niall Òg on the northern road* (Dùn dhearg). On a wet stretch of the northern road, Mòrag nan Rathad shelters from rain beside an old man on a milestone: Niall Òg, grandson of Ailean Mòr, now past his sixteen hundredth year. He tells her his name and sits with her a while before going on afoot.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0081"><em>Mòrag of the Roads</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, FE 754</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5026"><em>The toll-chest counted at a keeper's own door</em>, 18 an t-Iuchar, FE 756</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5028"></a>**19 an t-Ògmhios, FE 760** — *Niall Òg tells Mòrag of the cord* (Dùn dhearg). Niall Òg tells Mòrag nan Rathad of the cord of seven hundred and twelve knots laid on the floor at Dùn ìseal, and says she is the first of the line he has met who looks at the cord itself and not at her own knot in it.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0001a"><em>The heirs sit at Dùn ìseal</em>, 13 an Dàmhair, FE 1</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5027"><em>Mòrag meets Niall Òg on the northern road</em>, 25 am Faoilleach, FE 760</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5029"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, FE 763** — *The golden house opened free of toll* (Seann Dunn). Mòrag nan Rathad opens the new waypoint house on the eastern road north of Seann Dunn with a night's feast for every carrier who can be reached in time, none of them charged the toll. Carriers call the new timber the golden house before it has weathered, and the name holds.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5028"><em>Niall Òg tells Mòrag of the cord</em>, 19 an t-Ògmhios, FE 760</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0082"></a>**26 an t-Iuchar, FE 781** — *The golden house* (An Taigh-seinnse Òir). Mòrag nan Rathad has a waypoint house built on the road north of Seann Dunn, on the site of An Taigh-seinnse Òir, to shorten the carriers' stage from the coast to the mountain. It is the first waypoint house raised by a ruler and not by a family.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-5029"><em>The golden house opened free of toll</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, FE 763</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0083"></a>**24 an Lùnastal, FE 794** — *The bridge-foot rebuilt* (Drochaid Cathair dhearg). At the bidding of Mòrag nan Rathad the western crossing of the Abhainn dhomhain is rebuilt in wider stone, so that two laden carriers can pass on it. The hearth-sign of Ailean Clachair is cut again in its keystone. From this time the town at the bridge-foot begins to grow.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5030"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, FE 794** — *The bridge-foot town begins to grow* (Cathair dhearg). After the western crossing of the Abhainn dhomhain is widened for two laden carts abreast, the small fishing town at the bridge-foot below Dùn ìseal begins to grow in earnest, outgrowing three neighbouring towns within Mòrag nan Rathad's own lifetime.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0083"><em>The bridge-foot rebuilt</em>, 24 an Lùnastal, FE 794</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5029"><em>The golden house opened free of toll</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, FE 763</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5031"></a>**22 an Giblean, FE 800** — *Mòrag names Dòmhnall her heir* (Dùn dhearg). Mòrag nan Rathad has her lame son Dòmhnall carried the length of three road-stretches in a covered chair, then names him before the household at Dùn dhearg as her heir, past her hundred and sixtieth year herself.

## The Years FE 801 – 1,000

- <a id="ev-EIII-5032"></a>**25 am Faoilleach, FE 830** — *Mòrag's last circuit of the roads* (Dùn dhearg). Against the advice of her household, Mòrag nan Rathad rides the whole western circuit in her hundred and eighty-ninth year, finding less to mend than in any year of her reign, and tells the waypoint-keepers so at every house she stops in.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0081"><em>Mòrag of the Roads</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, FE 754</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5031"><em>Mòrag names Dòmhnall her heir</em>, 22 an Giblean, FE 800</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5033"></a>**14 am Faoilleach, FE 834** — *Mòrag nan Rathad dies at Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). Mòrag nan Rathad dies at Dùn dhearg in the winter, a hundred and ninety-four years old, with her son beside her. Carriers from three days' distance come to stand outside the hall, and Dòmhnall feeds them from the golden house's own stores.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0081"><em>Mòrag of the Roads</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, FE 754</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5032"><em>Mòrag's last circuit of the roads</em>, 25 am Faoilleach, FE 830</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0084"></a>**16 am Faoilleach, FE 834** — *Dòmhnall Crùbach* (Dùn dhearg). Dòmhnall Crùbach, Dòmhnall the Lame, follows his mother Mòrag at Dùn dhearg. He cannot walk the roads as she did, and rules through the keepers of the waypoint houses, who grow mighty in his reign.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5023"><em>Dòmhnall's fall from the cart</em>, 13 an Dàmhair, FE 736</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5031"><em>Mòrag names Dòmhnall her heir</em>, 22 an Giblean, FE 800</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5033"><em>Mòrag nan Rathad dies at Dùn dhearg</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, FE 834</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5034"></a>**20 an t-Ògmhios, FE 834** — *Niall Òg speaks over Mòrag's grave* (Dùn dhearg). At Mòrag nan Rathad's grave, Niall Òg says that of the seven hundred and twelve heirs he once watched knotted on the cord, she alone spent her life looking at the cord itself, and that her roads are the nearest thing since to that cord laid honestly on the ground.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0081"><em>Mòrag of the Roads</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, FE 754</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5033"><em>Mòrag nan Rathad dies at Dùn dhearg</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, FE 834</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5035"></a>**16 an Lùnastal, FE 860** — *Sìleas Dhonn finds the Ceann mhin rolls do not add* (Ceann mhin). Dòmhnall Crùbach's young niece Sìleas Dhonn, asked to check the waypoint-keepers' tallies, finds three years in which the Ceann mhin keepers' own count does not match what passed through their gates, though never provably by theft. She keeps her own copy of the figures and says nothing of it while her uncle lives.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5036"></a>**21 an Cèitean, FE 862** — *The scorpion's sting sworn on at a trade* (Baile àrsaidh). At Baile àrsaidh a woman stung on the hand during a trade of cattle for salt fish finishes the bargain with her fingers still swelling, saying a hurt taken in the open is worth more than a promise given behind a closed door. Others take up her way of it, keeping a dried sting in a box to swear by.
- <a id="ev-II-0085"></a>**14 an Gearran, FE 863** — *The waypoint-keepers of Ceann mhin* (Ceann mhin). In the reign of Dòmhnall Crùbach the keepers of the waypoint houses about the harbour town of Ceann mhin take the gathering of the road-toll into their own hands and pay the rìgh what they judge fair. Their judgement is generous to themselves, and the rolls keep the sums.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5035"><em>Sìleas Dhonn finds the Ceann mhin rolls do not add</em>, 16 an Lùnastal, FE 860</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0086"></a>**19 an t-Samhain, FE 879** — *Baile àrsaidh on the western heath* (Baile àrsaidh). Settlers from Cathair dhomhain take the wet heath of the west coast and found Baile àrsaidh, where the soil is thin and the yellow scorpions thick. They swear their oaths on a scorpion's sting kept in a box, and their neighbours think it a strange custom.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5036"><em>The scorpion's sting sworn on at a trade</em>, 21 an Cèitean, FE 862</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0087"></a>**18 an Dùbhlachd, FE 879** — *The storm at Seann Chwen* (Seann Chwen). A storm drives the sea over the harbour at Seann Chwen and takes the boats and a third of the houses. The Keeper sends the Hall's grain from Dùn ìseal, and Dòmhnall Crùbach sends his from Dùn dhearg. The survivors remember that the Hall's came first.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5037"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, FE 879** — *The Hall's grain-carts reach Seann Chwen first* (Dùn ìseal). After the storm at Seann Chwen, the Keeper's grain-carts reach the ruined harbour a full day ahead of Dòmhnall Crùbach's, running the whole way on the road above the ford that Mòrag nan Rathad raised out of the mud in the first summer of her reign.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0087"><em>The storm at Seann Chwen</em>, 18 an Dùbhlachd, FE 879</a>; ⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0081"><em>Mòrag of the Roads</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, FE 754</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5038"></a>**4 an Lùnastal, FE 880** — *The sting first sworn on at a wider trade* (Baile àrsaidh). The scorpion's-sting oath of Baile àrsaidh is sworn for the first time at a trade with an outside harbour town, at Ros bheag, carrying the custom beyond the settlement that began it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0086"><em>Baile àrsaidh on the western heath</em>, 19 an t-Samhain, FE 879</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5039"></a>**2 an t-Sultain, FE 880** — *Rònat sent to the stag's school* (Muileann chiar). A boy of ten with a talent for losing count past thirty is sent from his father's holding to the stag's school in the holy wood east of Muileann chiar. Aonghas Cam, the old cutter, scores his first tally-stick through the middle and sets him cutting sticks two years before he is trusted near a beast to be counted.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5040"></a>**20 am Màrt, FE 901** — *Aonghas Cam's failing thread* (Muileann chiar). A fever settles in the old cutter's crooked leg and will not draw out. Through that winter Rònat watches him grope after names and lines of the long teaching-thread and not always find them, and it is by that fireside, and not by any beast to be counted, that the shape of the sound-marks first comes to him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5039"><em>Rònat sent to the stag's school</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, FE 880</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5041"></a>**19 an Gearran, FE 902** — *The first name cut in strokes* (Muileann chiar). Rònat cuts his own name onto a length of ash by a scheme of small strokes, one to a sound, and reads it back cold three days after. He sets the same trick to Aonghas Cam's own name and lays the stick in the old man's hand, who reads his name off it and calls it a count of sounds where he had always cut a count of fish.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5040"><em>Aonghas Cam's failing thread</em>, 20 am Màrt, FE 901</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5042"></a>**21 am Faoilleach, FE 903** — *The death of Aonghas Cam* (Muileann chiar). The old cutter of Muileann chiar's stag school dies in his sleep, having asked that his own years be counted the old way at the last, one stroke to a year, having spent his life trusting a count over a name. Rònat cuts the tally himself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5041"><em>The first name cut in strokes</em>, 19 an Gearran, FE 902</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5043"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, FE 905** — *The western teachers come east* (Muileann chiar). Two teachers of the western druid school travel to the far-eastern Muileann chiar to learn Rònat's sound-marks, and stay a season under a man twenty years their junior. Among them is Sìleas nic Ruairidh, eldest of the two, who carries the scheme home and turns it over in her own mind.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5042"><em>The death of Aonghas Cam</em>, 21 am Faoilleach, FE 903</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5044"></a>**15 an t-Ògmhios, FE 908** — *The letters set against the obelisk* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). Rònat and two others walk five days east to the grey stone at Cnoc bheag and set the sound-marks stroke for stroke against the old marks cut there. Nothing answers: no vowel, no grouping, no order in the stone's marks matches theirs.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5043"><em>The western teachers come east</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, FE 905</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5045"></a>**14 an t-Iuchar, FE 908** — *The first thing written of the old marks* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). Before the road home, Rònat cuts onto ash the finding at Cnoc bheag: that the makers of the old stone did not teach the makers of the stag's marks and are not known to them. It is the first thought, rather than a name or a count, that the new marks are made to carry.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5044"><em>The letters set against the obelisk</em>, 15 an t-Ògmhios, FE 908</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5046"></a>**18 an Giblean, FE 912** — *Niall Òg at the stag's school* (Muileann chiar). The ancient heir passes through the far east on foot and sits two evenings by the school's fire, telling pupils tales of the night of the handful. He asks, at the second evening's end, after the trick of marks he has heard tell of on the road.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5045"><em>The first thing written of the old marks</em>, 14 an t-Iuchar, FE 908</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5047"></a>**17 an Cèitean, FE 912** — *Niall Òg reads his own name* (Muileann chiar). Rònat cuts Niall Òg's name in the sound-marks and sets the stick in his hand. The old heir, who has been called by his name more times than there are fish in the western sea, reads it back within the hour and laughs until he coughs, saying he has found, at last, a name that stays after the mouth that gave it has gone home.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5046"><em>Niall Òg at the stag's school</em>, 18 an Giblean, FE 912</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0088"></a>**15 am Màrt, FE 914** — *The stag-letters* (Muileann chiar). At Muileann chiar in the far east the teachers of the stag's people make the cutters' tally-notches into signs for sounds, so that a teaching may be kept without a teacher. These are the first letters the Dia-thìrich use: the ogham, which the druids call the gift of Ogma.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5039"><em>Rònat sent to the stag's school</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, FE 880</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5040"><em>Aonghas Cam's failing thread</em>, 20 am Màrt, FE 901</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5041"><em>The first name cut in strokes</em>, 19 an Gearran, FE 902</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-5042"><em>The death of Aonghas Cam</em>, 21 am Faoilleach, FE 903</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-5043"><em>The western teachers come east</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, FE 905</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0089"></a>**12 an Cèitean, FE 914** — *The letters set against the obelisk* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). Scholars of the stag carry their new letters to Carragh Cnoc bheag and set them beside the marks on the obelisk. They match nothing. The scholars write that the stone's makers were not their teachers, and that is the first thing the Dia-thìrich ever write of the old people.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5044"><em>The letters set against the obelisk</em>, 15 an t-Ògmhios, FE 908</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-5045"><em>The first thing written of the old marks</em>, 14 an t-Iuchar, FE 908</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5048"></a>**26 an Cèitean, FE 914** — *The chest of mismatched tallies opened* (Dùn dhearg). Sìleas Dhonn, new in the chair at Dùn dhearg after Dòmhnall Crùbach's death, has brought out and opened before the household the chest she has kept locked for years: her own fair copy of three seasons' Ceann mhin tallies that never matched the toll counted at the gate.
- <a id="ev-II-0090"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, FE 914** — *Sìleas Dhonn* (Dùn dhearg). Sìleas Dhonn, niece of Dòmhnall Crùbach, holds Dùn dhearg after him. In her reign the keepers of the waypoint houses are bidden to render account of the tolls at her hall once a year, and several of them do.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5035"><em>Sìleas Dhonn finds the Ceann mhin rolls do not add</em>, 16 an Lùnastal, FE 860</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5048"><em>The chest of mismatched tallies opened</em>, 26 an Cèitean, FE 914</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5049"></a>**4 an Giblean, FE 915** — *Beathan mac Dhonnchaidh's memory found wanting* (Muileann shean). The old keeper of Muileann shean recites his tally to Sìleas Dhonn from memory, the old way, name for name; she asks him plainly how she is to know it is the same tally he gave the road-guard three seasons past. He has no answer beyond his own honesty, and she sends east for a teacher of the sound-marks.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0090"><em>Sìleas Dhonn</em>, 10 an t-Ògmhios, FE 914</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5048"><em>The chest of mismatched tallies opened</em>, 26 an Cèitean, FE 914</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5050"></a>**2 an t-Iuchar, FE 915** — *Rònat teaches Sìleas Dhonn's clerks* (Dùn dhearg). Rònat walks the last long road of his active years to Dùn dhearg and teaches the ruler's clerks the sound-marks over a winter, finding grown clerks trained to a column of figures quicker with the knife than any pupil he taught in the holy wood.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0090"><em>Sìleas Dhonn</em>, 10 an t-Ògmhios, FE 914</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5049"><em>Beathan mac Dhonnchaidh's memory found wanting</em>, 4 an Giblean, FE 915</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5051"></a>**3 an Cèitean, FE 916** — *Ailig mac Ruairidh caught by his own gate* (Ceann mhin). The keeper of Ceann mhin's toll, first summoned to render account cut in the new marks and checked against the road-guard's own cutting at his gate, is found short by a sum no honest forgetting explains. It is the first time a keeper's own tally, and not his word, answers for him before the hall.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0090"><em>Sìleas Dhonn</em>, 10 an t-Ògmhios, FE 914</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5050"><em>Rònat teaches Sìleas Dhonn's clerks</em>, 2 an t-Iuchar, FE 915</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5052"></a>**1 an t-Ògmhios, FE 916** — *The first whole sentence* (Dùn dhearg). Cutting the record of Ailig mac Ruairidh's shortfall for the hall's keeping, Rònat sets down the first whole sentence any hand has yet cut in the sound-marks: that the toll of Ceann mhin was counted short and the keeper answered for it. It stands after him in the hall, saying the same thing to every thumb that reads it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0090"><em>Sìleas Dhonn</em>, 10 an t-Ògmhios, FE 914</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5051"><em>Ailig mac Ruairidh caught by his own gate</em>, 3 an Cèitean, FE 916</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0091"></a>**14 an Gearran, FE 991** — *The lords of Caol leathan* (Caol leathan). The harbour town of Caol leathan in the south-west grows rich on the western fishing and the southern end of the carriers' road. Its leading family, under Lachlann Ciar, takes the road-toll for itself and sends none of it to Dùn dhearg.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5053"></a>**17 an Giblean, FE 994** — *Sìleas Dhonn dies at her ledger* (Dùn dhearg). Sìleas Dhonn dies in the chair at Dùn dhearg with a keeper's tally open on her knee, in her hundred and ninety-fourth year. She has asked that the chair stand its customary night and day and no longer, having had forty years at her uncle's side to learn the feel of it.
- <a id="ev-II-0092"></a>**12 an Cèitean, FE 994** — *Iain Garbh* (Dùn dhearg). Iain Garbh, Iain the Rough, son of Sìleas Dhonn, takes the hall at Dùn dhearg and demands the western tolls of Caol leathan. Lachlann Ciar sends back a basket of fish-bones.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5053"><em>Sìleas Dhonn dies at her ledger</em>, 17 an Giblean, FE 994</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5054"></a>**28 an t-Samhain, FE 994** — *Iain Garbh's demand sent south* (Dùn dhearg). On his first morning in the chair Iain Garbh reads Caol leathan's thin account and sends a rider south with a plain demand in his own hand: the toll owed in full, counted before Dùn dhearg's own man at the harbour, or an answer for why it should not be paid.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0092"><em>Iain Garbh</em>, 12 an Cèitean, FE 994</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5053"><em>Sìleas Dhonn dies at her ledger</em>, 17 an Giblean, FE 994</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5055"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, FE 994** — *The basket set on the hall floor* (Dùn dhearg). Iain Garbh's rider returns from Caol leathan white about the mouth, carrying a covered basket he will not open himself. Iain lifts the lid to find it packed in rows with fish-bones, picked clean, and no letter with it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0092"><em>Iain Garbh</em>, 12 an Cèitean, FE 994</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5054"><em>Iain Garbh's demand sent south</em>, 28 an t-Samhain, FE 994</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-5056"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, FE 994** — *Iain Garbh calls the levy* (Dùn dhearg). Iain Garbh laughs once over the basket of fish-bones, then calls the road-guards from every waypoint within three days' ride and tells the lowland households their levy stands, raising his voice at no one the whole of that week.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5055"><em>The basket set on the hall floor</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, FE 994</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0093"></a>**13 an Giblean, FE 999** — *The War of the Roads begins at Muileann òg* (Muileann òg). Iain Garbh marches west with the road-guards and the lowland levies, and burns the toll-house at Muileann òg that the men of Lachlann Ciar had taken. It is the first war of Dia-thìreach against Dia-thìreach since the Peace of the Threshold, and the first fought over a road; every war before it was fought over a share. The Hall will bless neither side.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-5056"><em>Iain Garbh calls the levy</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, FE 994</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0094"></a>**19 an t-Samhain, FE 1,000** — *Uisdean mac Ruairidh's refusal* (Dùn ìseal). The Keeper Uisdean mac Ruairidh refuses the messengers of Iain Garbh at Dùn ìseal the Hall's handful for the warband's hearths, saying that the flame does not warm men who go out to kill. The warband winters on peat. Iain Garbh never forgives the Hall, and never enters it.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5057"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,000** — *Iain Garbh folds the Keeper's answer* (Dùn ìseal). Iain Garbh's messengers return from Dùn ìseal empty-handed, made to repeat Uisdean mac Ruairidh's refusal word for word. Iain folds the written answer once and puts it inside his coat, and never again sets foot on the Hall's ground.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0094"><em>Uisdean mac Ruairidh's refusal</em>, 19 an t-Samhain, FE 1,000</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5056"><em>Iain Garbh calls the levy</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, FE 994</a>.</span>

## The Years FE 1,001 – 1,200

- <a id="ev-II-0095"></a>**21 an Dàmhair, FE 1,001** — *The fight at Àth fhiadhaich* (Àth fhiadhaich). The men of Caol leathan meet the levies of Iain Garbh at the ford of Àth fhiadhaich and hold it for a day before they give way. Forty lie dead of both sides. Long afterwards the carriers call it the ford of the forty.
- <a id="ev-EIII-5058"></a>**28 an t-Samhain, FE 1,001** — *The coughing winter at Muileann òg* (Muileann òg). The warband winters on peat smoke at the burned toll-house of Muileann òg. Men who marched south whole come home in spring with a cough some of them carry the rest of their days, so that the older road-guards are known ever after by the sound of a hard winter's night.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0094"><em>Uisdean mac Ruairidh's refusal</em>, 19 an t-Samhain, FE 1,000</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5057"><em>Iain Garbh folds the Keeper's answer</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,000</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0096"></a>**16 am Faoilleach, FE 1,002** — *Baile ghlas burned* (Baile ghlas). The men of Lachlann Ciar, falling back on Caol leathan, burn Baile ghlas, that the levies of Iain Garbh may find no grain. Its people walk to Cathair dhomhain, and many never return.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6001"></a>**28 an Lùnastal, FE 1,002** — *The unnamed man of the ford* (Àth fhiadhaich). At the ford of Àth fhiadhaich a man of Caol leathan holds a split shield upright well past any sense left in the holding, until a spear from behind Iain Garbh's own rank finds him. No name is ever kept for him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0095"><em>The fight at Àth fhiadhaich</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, FE 1,001</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-5058"><em>The coughing winter at Muileann òg</em>, 28 an t-Samhain, FE 1,001</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0097"></a>**18 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,003** — *Baile chiar holds* (Baile chiar). Baile chiar, south of the western bridge-foot, shuts its gate on both hosts in the War of the Roads and feeds the burned-out folk of Baile ghlas through the winter. Neither side forgives it, and neither attacks it.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6002"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,003** — *Beathag of Baile chiar turns back a spear* (Baile chiar). Riding to Baile chiar for a night's lodging, Iain Garbh is met on the wall by the town's reeve, Beathag, who will open the gate to the hungry and to no one carrying a spear. He leaves the spear on the road and sleeps that night among the burned-out of Baile ghlas.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0097"><em>Baile chiar holds</em>, 18 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,003</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6001"><em>The unnamed man of the ford</em>, 28 an Lùnastal, FE 1,002</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0098"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, FE 1,005** — *The siege of Caol leathan* (Caol leathan). Iain Garbh shuts Caol leathan in from the land for a season, but its boats bring in fish from the sea, and the harbour he cannot close. His levies begin to go home for the harvest, and the siege ends without an assault.
- <a id="ev-II-0099"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, FE 1,006** — *The peace at Mòr nic Dhùghaill's house* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). Iain Garbh and Lachlann Ciar meet under the roof of the waypoint house that is afterwards Am Buabhall Fortanach, where by the road-peace neither may draw. Caol leathan keeps half its tolls and sends half to Dùn dhearg, and Lachlann Ciar swears to the Law before the Keeper's witness. So the War of the Roads ends in a house built to feed carriers.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6003"></a>**28 an Gearran, FE 1,008** — *Lachlann Ciar's confession at the peace-board* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). At the waypoint house on the road-peace, Lachlann Ciar tells Iain Garbh that the basket of fish-bones was his son's notion, sent out under his own name because a father does not answer for a son's foolishness by naming him. The two talk the evening out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0099"><em>The peace at Mòr nic Dhùghaill's house</em>, 4 an Dàmhair, FE 1,006</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6002"><em>Beathag of Baile chiar turns back a spear</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,003</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0100"></a>**12 am Faoilleach, FE 1,009** — *The wolf-sworn of Caol leathan* (Caol leathan). Men who fought for Caol leathan become its road-guards and swear their watch on a white stone carved as a wolf, kept at the town gate. They call themselves the wolf-sworn.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6004"></a>**29 an Cèitean, FE 1,009** — *Iain Garbh witnesses the wolf-sworn* (Caol leathan). At Lachlann Ciar's own asking, Iain Garbh rides south to stand at the gate of Caol leathan while the men of its siege swear their new watch on a white stone cut as a wolf, and are called from that day the wolf-sworn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0100"><em>The wolf-sworn of Caol leathan</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, FE 1,009</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6003"><em>Lachlann Ciar's confession at the peace-board</em>, 28 an Gearran, FE 1,008</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6005"></a>**21 an Lùnastal, FE 1,010** — *News of the fish-bone war reaches Cathair mhòr* (Cathair mhòr). A wool-merchant brings Eithne nic Ailein, last living of the nine who cut the cord at the Roinn, the tale of Iain Garbh's war on Caol leathan. She does not ride to it and does not send to it, judging it another share's quarrel to end.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6006"></a>**26 an Cèitean, FE 1,011** — *Word of the harbour wall at Caol fhiadhaich* (Caol fhiadhaich). The wool-merchant's next journey brings word to Cathair mhòr of how Caol fhiadhaich fed besieged Caol leathan by night and was given a share of the western tolls, with which it raised the first stone wall that coast has had. Eithne asks after the wall every year after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6005"><em>News of the fish-bone war reaches Cathair mhòr</em>, 21 an Lùnastal, FE 1,010</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6007"></a>**24 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,020** — *Lachlann Ciar dies within sight of the harbour* (Caol leathan). Lachlann Ciar dies in his ninetieth year, worn down by slow degrees by the cough he carried from the coughing winter. His household buries him within sight of the harbour he grew fat and then thin defending, his son standing at the peace-board in his place.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0099"><em>The peace at Mòr nic Dhùghaill's house</em>, 4 an Dàmhair, FE 1,006</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6004"><em>Iain Garbh witnesses the wolf-sworn</em>, 29 an Cèitean, FE 1,009</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0101"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,036** — *Caol fhiadhaich rebuilt* (Caol fhiadhaich). Caol fhiadhaich on the south-western shore had sent its boats to feed Caol leathan through the siege. In thanks Lachlann Ciar gives it a share of the western tolls, and with it the town builds a harbour wall.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-EIII-6005"><em>News of the fish-bone war reaches Cathair mhòr</em>, 21 an Lùnastal, FE 1,010</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-6006"><em>Word of the harbour wall at Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 26 an Cèitean, FE 1,011</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6008"></a>**4 an t-Sultain, FE 1,044** — *Iain Garbh never climbs to the cup* (Dùn dhearg). Iain Garbh rules forty years past the end of the War of the Roads and never once goes up the mountain road to stand before the cup, unlike every rìgh before or after him. He dies unreconciled to the flame that had refused his warband its blessing.
- <a id="ev-II-0102"></a>**15 an t-Samhain, FE 1,044** — *Death of Iain Garbh* (Dùn dhearg). Iain Garbh dies at Dùn dhearg. His daughter Catrìona buries him in the floor of the hall and not on the slope at Dùn ìseal, and the Hall does not ask for him.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-6008"><em>Iain Garbh never climbs to the cup</em>, 4 an t-Sultain, FE 1,044</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6009"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,044** — *Catrìona Ghlic crowned at Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). Catrìona, daughter of Iain Garbh, is crowned at Dùn dhearg on her father's death and takes within ten years the name Catrìona Ghlic, Catrìona the Wise, for undoing the coldness he had left between the rìgh's hall and the Hall of the Flame.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0102"><em>Death of Iain Garbh</em>, 15 an t-Samhain, FE 1,044</a>.</span>
