- <a id="ev-II-0103"></a>**17 an Dàmhair, FE 1,046** — *Catrìona Ghlic* (Dùn dhearg). Catrìona Ghlic, Catrìona the Wise, rules from Dùn dhearg. She sends her own son to sit a season with the flame, the first child of the royal house to do so since the division of keeping. By the end of her reign the Hall and the hall are on speaking terms again.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6010"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, FE 1,051** — *The rìgh's tithe sent again to the Hall* (Cathair mhòr). Eithne nic Ailein, hearing that Catrìona Ghlic's son has sat a season with the flame unasked, orders that Cathair mhòr's own hall send its tithe to the Hall's handful again, unwaited-for, as it had not done since her own father's day.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-II-0103"><em>Catrìona Ghlic</em>, 17 an Dàmhair, FE 1,046</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6009"><em>Catrìona Ghlic crowned at Dùn dhearg</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,044</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6011"></a>**21 an Lùnastal, FE 1,058** — *The Keeper keeps a place for the rìgh's son* (Dùn ìseal). After his first season carrying the baskets at Dùn ìseal, Catrìona Ghlic's son returns each year at the turn of the season, and the Keeper comes to keep a place for him at the long table without being asked, a small thing the island reads as the breach mended.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0103"><em>Catrìona Ghlic</em>, 17 an Dàmhair, FE 1,046</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6010"><em>The rìgh's tithe sent again to the Hall</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, FE 1,051</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6012"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, FE 1,075** — *Inis mhòr asks the crown for its own guard* (Inis mhòr). The wool port of Inis mhòr, grown past every other town in the north on the trade the two new waypoint houses carry, asks Catrìona Ghlic's crown for a road-guard of its own, and is given one without argument.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6011"><em>The Keeper keeps a place for the rìgh's son</em>, 21 an Lùnastal, FE 1,058</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0104"></a>**8 an Cèitean, FE 1,081** — *The house on the northern road* (An Leòmhann Buidhe). Catrìona Ghlic has a waypoint house built on the northern road above Inis mhòr, on the site of An Leòmhann Buidhe. It serves the carriers who take the Hall's baskets to the northern households and bring back wool.
- <a id="ev-II-0105"></a>**9 an Giblean, FE 1,085** — *The house on the cold road* (An Taigh-seinnse Reòta). A stone house is built on the open moor, on the road between Baile Mòr dhomhain and the northern coast, on the site of An Taigh-seinnse Reòta, for carriers caught by snow. The Hall pays its keepers in grain and the crown in cloth, and they complain of both.
- <a id="ev-II-0106"></a>**11 am Màrt, FE 1,089** — *Inis mhòr grows* (Inis mhòr). The river port of Inis mhòr in the north becomes the gathering-place of the northern wool trade and outgrows every other northern town. Its people ask Catrìona Ghlic for a road-guard of their own, and are given one.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-6012"><em>Inis mhòr asks the crown for its own guard</em>, 16 an t-Samhain, FE 1,075</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6013"></a>**27 an Giblean, FE 1,109** — *Niall Òg walks his last road* (Cathair mhòr). Niall Òg comes on foot and unannounced to Eithne nic Ailein's hall at Cathair mhòr, the last road he means to walk, so that the night of the handful should be told once more, to the only other living witness of it, before he dies.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6014"></a>**26 an Cèitean, FE 1,109** — *Death of Niall Òg* (Cathair mhòr). Niall Òg dies in his sleep by Eithne nic Ailein's own fire at Cathair mhòr, some two thousand years old, three days after telling her the night of the handful for what proves the last time. She sends his body up the mountain at her own cost.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6013"><em>Niall Òg walks his last road</em>, 27 an Giblean, FE 1,109</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6015"></a>**18 an Dàmhair, FE 1,109** — *Niall Òg laid near the first heirs* (Dùn ìseal). Eithne has Niall Òg laid near the old graves on the slope below Dùn ìseal, among the first heirs of the Roinn, though he was of no kin to her own share, judging that a man who spent four hundred years walking every road on the island had earned the ground.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6014"><em>Death of Niall Òg</em>, 26 an Cèitean, FE 1,109</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6016"></a>**23 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,121** — *Eithne asks the count of her own years* (Cathair mhòr). In her last year Eithne nic Ailein asks her steward more than once to reckon the exact tale of her days, wanting the number fixed precisely at the end, though her mind has not begun to fail her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6015"><em>Niall Òg laid near the first heirs</em>, 18 an Dàmhair, FE 1,109</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0106b"></a>**28 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,122** — *Death of Eithne nic Ailein, last of the nine* (Cathair mhòr). Eithne nic Ailein, daughter of Ailean Mòr and youngest of the nine who took the great shares at the Roinn, dies in her hall at Cathair mhòr. And all the days of Eithne were three thousand and twenty-one years, and she died. After her none of the nine is living, and the great shares are names on the boundary stones.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-6016"><em>Eithne asks the count of her own years</em>, 23 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,121</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0106a"></a>**22 an t-Samhain, FE 1,122** — *The market at the fords of Baile Mòr dhomhain* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). The lords of the deep river set a market at Baile Mòr dhomhain, where the carriers' road from the south meets the paths down from the hill pastures. Cattle, sheep, horses, hides and the white stone of the hills are sold at the fords on the day after each new moon, and the lords take one fleece in forty from the sellers.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6017"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,122** — *Eithne's hall at Cathair mhòr falls silent* (Cathair mhòr). With Eithne nic Ailein's death her hall at Cathair mhòr is left to her stewards and her reciters, who keep the rolls but crown no one there, the lowland share having long since ceased to answer to any single hand of her line.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0106b"><em>Death of Eithne nic Ailein, last of the nine</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,122</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6016"><em>Eithne asks the count of her own years</em>, 23 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,121</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6018"></a>**9 an Cèitean, FE 1,123** — *The mill at Muileann shean* (Muileann shean). A mill is raised on the northern road at Muileann shean to grind grain for the carriers crossing the pass; the miller pays the Hall in grain and the rìgh's toll in flour, and a town grows round the mill within two generations.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6019"></a>**10 an Giblean, FE 1,124** — *Catrìona Ghlic dies at a hundred and twenty-two* (Dùn dhearg). Catrìona Ghlic, who mended the breach her father Iain Garbh's war had opened, dies at Dùn dhearg. Her son takes the hall at ninety-two, the first of eleven rulers the later king-list will give only by name and order.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0103"><em>Catrìona Ghlic</em>, 17 an Dàmhair, FE 1,046</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6020"></a>**29 an Lùnastal, FE 1,130** — *The Hall's own roll for the same years* (Dùn ìseal). For the span the king-list gives eleven rulers, the Hall's spoken roll gives only five Keepers, a mountain's years running longer than a lowland's, as every teller of the Fire already knows.
- <a id="ev-II-0107"></a>**10 an Gearran, FE 1,166** — *Muileann shean on the northern road* (Muileann shean). A mill is built at Muileann shean on the northern road, to grind the grain the carriers bring over the pass, and a town grows round it. The Hall pays the miller in grain, and he pays the rìgh's toll in flour.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-6018"><em>The mill at Muileann shean</em>, 9 an Cèitean, FE 1,123</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6021"></a>**27 an t-Sultain, FE 1,190** — *The last of the long years in the ruling line* (Dùn dhearg). The last ruler of the house of Ìomhar and Goraidh to carry any of the long years in his blood dies at a hundred years old, an age that was a boy's age in his grandmother's grandmother's day. After him the line ages and dies at the pace of any household on the island.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0098a"><em>Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, FE 1</a>.</span>

## The Years FE 1,201 – 1,400

- <a id="ev-II-0108"></a>**1 an t-Sultain, FE 1,211** — *The unremembered rulers* (Dùn dhearg). Eleven rulers hold Dùn dhearg between Catrìona Ghlic and Ealasaid Chiar. The later king-list gives their names and their order, and nothing more. For the same years the Keepers' roll gives five Keepers, and of them too only the names.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EIII-6020"><em>The Hall's own roll for the same years</em>, 29 an Lùnastal, FE 1,130</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6022"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, FE 1,240** — *Tormod mac Iain born to the house of Tormod* (Dùn dhearg). Tormod is born at Dùn dhearg, a younger son of a house that has held no great office in the hall for three generations. His father Iain keeps a stretch of the crown granaries, and the boy grows up among grain-tallies.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6023"></a>**14 an Cèitean, FE 1,255** — *Tormod sent east to Muileann chiar* (Muileann chiar). A passing stag-teacher's tale of letters that can hold a teaching without a teacher fixes itself in the fifteen-year-old Tormod's mind. His father, a younger son's post being cheaper found elsewhere than at home, sends him east to Muileann chiar to learn the stag-letters.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6022"><em>Tormod mac Iain born to the house of Tormod</em>, 26 an Dàmhair, FE 1,240</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0109"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, FE 1,255** — *Tormod Scrìobhaiche learns the letters* (Muileann chiar). Tormod mac Iain, a younger son of the house of Tormod, is sent east to Muileann chiar to learn the stag-letters. He is the first of the royal kin to read, and for the rest of his life he is called Tormod Scrìobhaiche, Tormod the Writer.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-6022"><em>Tormod mac Iain born to the house of Tormod</em>, 26 an Dàmhair, FE 1,240</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-6023"><em>Tormod sent east to Muileann chiar</em>, 14 an Cèitean, FE 1,255</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6024"></a>**5 an Cèitean, FE 1,256** — *Tormod's first written leaf* (Muileann chiar). In his second summer at Muileann chiar, Tormod writes his first whole leaf, a grain-debt tally copied twice over from an old woman's spoken account. He keeps it inside his shirt a full year, the oldest surviving thing in his own hand.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0109"><em>Tormod Scrìobhaiche learns the letters</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, FE 1,255</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6023"><em>Tormod sent east to Muileann chiar</em>, 14 an Cèitean, FE 1,255</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6025"></a>**3 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,259** — *Tormod returns to the granaries* (Dùn dhearg). After four years at Muileann chiar, Tormod comes home to Dùn dhearg and his father's trade of the granaries, carrying unspoken a want to write down a thing that would outlast every mouth that had ever spoken it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0109"><em>Tormod Scrìobhaiche learns the letters</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, FE 1,255</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6024"><em>Tormod's first written leaf</em>, 5 an Cèitean, FE 1,256</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0110"></a>**22 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,299** — *Ealasaid Chiar* (Dùn dhearg). Ealasaid Chiar takes the hall at Dùn dhearg and brings Tormod Scrìobhaiche there as her clerk. She bids him set down in order the name of every ruler of the hall that the reciters can give him.
- <a id="ev-II-0111"></a>**20 an Lùnastal, FE 1,299** — *The first written king-list*. Rulers are first set down by name, and no longer only remembered in tales. The rolls of succession in every later age are kept after this pattern.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6026"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, FE 1,299** — *Ealasaid Chiar takes the hall* (Dùn dhearg). Ealasaid Chiar, granddaughter of the ninth of the eleven, takes the hall at Dùn dhearg at twenty-nine, out of patience with hearing her own house's roll given a different order at every telling.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0110"><em>Ealasaid Chiar</em>, 22 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,299</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6027"></a>**8 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,299** — *Ealasaid Chiar sets Tormod to the writing* (Dùn dhearg). Ealasaid Chiar hears of a granary clerk who can set a thing down in marks and have it read back the same way twice, and sets Tormod Scrìobhaiche, now fifty-nine, to write down every ruler the reciters can name, in order, freed of all other duty.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0110"><em>Ealasaid Chiar</em>, 22 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,299</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6026"><em>Ealasaid Chiar takes the hall</em>, 4 an Dàmhair, FE 1,299</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0112"></a>**18 an t-Sultain, FE 1,300** — *The contents of Tormod's roll* (Dùn dhearg). Tormod Scrìobhaiche's roll, kept in the hall at Dùn dhearg, runs from Goraidh Mòr to Ealasaid Chiar. The earlier names he has from the reciters and the later from living memory, and he marks which are which. In three places it differs from the Keepers' spoken roll; Tormod writes down both readings and does not choose.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6028"></a>**9 am Faoilleach, FE 1,301** — *The reciters disagree* (Dùn dhearg). Questioning the hall's reciters in turn, Tormod finds them certain and contradictory: a mother's name given two ways, a reign given nine years by one mouth and eleven by another, three rulers set in different orders by a southern reciter than by the hall's own.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0112"><em>The contents of Tormod's roll</em>, 18 an t-Sultain, FE 1,300</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6027"><em>Ealasaid Chiar sets Tormod to the writing</em>, 8 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,299</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6029"></a>**7 an Gearran, FE 1,301** — *Ealasaid Chiar bids the doubt be written too* (Dùn dhearg). Told of the disagreements, Ealasaid Chiar orders Tormod to set down the sure thing where he has it and the doubt where he has that, rather than hide the roll's own uncertainty from those who could not otherwise judge it.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0112"><em>The contents of Tormod's roll</em>, 18 an t-Sultain, FE 1,300</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6028"><em>The reciters disagree</em>, 9 am Faoilleach, FE 1,301</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6030"></a>**19 an Gearran, FE 1,305** — *Tormod's roll finished* (Dùn dhearg). After six years' careful writing, reading each page back to whoever gave it before counting it done, Tormod brings Ealasaid Chiar the finished roll from Goraidh Mòr to herself, with three disputed places marked and left unresolved.<span class="fn fl">✦ Fulfils <a href="#ev-II-0111"><em>The first written king-list</em>, 20 an Lùnastal, FE 1,299</a>; ✦ Fulfils <a href="#ev-II-0112"><em>The contents of Tormod's roll</em>, 18 an t-Sultain, FE 1,300</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6029"><em>Ealasaid Chiar bids the doubt be written too</em>, 7 an Gearran, FE 1,301</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6031"></a>**21 am Faoilleach, FE 1,310** — *Death of Tormod Scrìobhaiche* (Dùn dhearg). Tormod Scrìobhaiche dies at seventy in the clerk's room off the hall at Dùn dhearg, a half-begun copy of the disputed reign still under his hand. Ealasaid Chiar names the room, ever after, Tormod's room.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0109"><em>Tormod Scrìobhaiche learns the letters</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, FE 1,255</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6030"><em>Tormod's roll finished</em>, 19 an Gearran, FE 1,305</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6032"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,311** — *The Hall shamed into writing its own roll* (Dùn ìseal). Word of the written king-list reaches the blind Keeper on the mountain, who sits three days in silence and then tells the Hall's own reciters that a Hall out-remembered by a rìgh's clerk has no one to blame but itself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6031"><em>Death of Tormod Scrìobhaiche</em>, 21 am Faoilleach, FE 1,310</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0113"></a>**17 an Dàmhair, FE 1,320** — *The Keepers' roll written down* (Dùn ìseal). Shamed, in the Hall's own words, by the rìgh's clerk, the Keepers have their spoken roll written in stag-letters at Dùn ìseal. It begins with Beathag Bhàn, and it is longer than Tormod's by several centuries.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-6032"><em>The Hall shamed into writing its own roll</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,311</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6033"></a>**30 an Dàmhair, FE 1,320** — *Cairistìona reads the cord for the scribes* (Dùn ìseal). Cairistìona nan Snaidhm, last of Sìne's line who can read a knot without letters, comes to the Hall and unties the cord of the heirs knot by knot over two days, naming each heir aloud so a young scribe can set the roll down in the new marks.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0113"><em>The Keepers' roll written down</em>, 17 an Dàmhair, FE 1,320</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6032"><em>The Hall shamed into writing its own roll</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,311</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6034"></a>**30 an t-Samhain, FE 1,320** — *The cord coiled in its chest* (Dùn ìseal). The last of the cord's seven hundred and twelve knots comes free, and Cairistìona coils it in the old way and lays it in the chest the Hall has made for it, telling the scribe that after her no hand living will be able to make it speak.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0113"><em>The Keepers' roll written down</em>, 17 an Dàmhair, FE 1,320</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6033"><em>Cairistìona reads the cord for the scribes</em>, 30 an Dàmhair, FE 1,320</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6035"></a>**27 an t-Sultain, FE 1,330** — *The death of Ealasaid Chiar* (Dùn dhearg). Ealasaid Chiar dies at sixty, having reigned thirty-one years and had the first king-list written, and is carried up the mountain road to lie among the house of Ìomhar. Her son takes the hall after her.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0110"><em>Ealasaid Chiar</em>, 22 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,299</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6036"></a>**29 an Lùnastal, FE 1,341** — *The roll falls silent* (Dùn ìseal). After Ealasaid Chiar's son and granddaughter, the king-list Tormod began keeps no ruler's name for a span the reciters cannot close. The Keepers' roll at Dùn ìseal keeps its own count through the same years, naming its Keepers where the hall names none.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0113"><em>The Keepers' roll written down</em>, 17 an Dàmhair, FE 1,320</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6035"><em>The death of Ealasaid Chiar</em>, 27 an t-Sultain, FE 1,330</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6037"></a>**31 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,380** — *The Hall's clerks learn the stag-letters* (Dùn ìseal). Shamed that it cannot read its own roll without borrowing another order's letters, the Hall at Dùn ìseal sets two of its own clerks to learn the stag-letters, taught by a stag-teacher paid in coal for the winter. From that year the Hall keeps its roll in its own hand.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-II-0113"><em>The Keepers' roll written down</em>, 17 an Dàmhair, FE 1,320</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6036"><em>The roll falls silent</em>, 29 an Lùnastal, FE 1,341</a>.</span>

## The Years FE 1,401 – 1,600

- <a id="ev-EIII-6038"></a>**2 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,440** — *A Keeper named in the silent years* (Dùn ìseal). A Keeper is named at Dùn ìseal of whom the roll keeps only the years of her reign, twenty-two, and the year of her death; of the rest of it nothing is told, the households burning their handful and the carriers walking their roads as their grandparents had.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0113"><em>The Keepers' roll written down</em>, 17 an Dàmhair, FE 1,320</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6037"><em>The Hall's clerks learn the stag-letters</em>, 31 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,380</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6039"></a>**3 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,540** — *The birth of Conall Dubh* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). A household above Cnoc bheag, keeping sheep in sight of the wood the island has never cleared, has its fourth child, a son they name Conall and call Dubh for the black hair he is born with.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6040"></a>**23 am Màrt, FE 1,560** — *Conall Dubh sees the black horned beast* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). At twenty years old, going up before first light to bring down strayed ewes, Conall Dubh meets a black horned beast at the edge of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, standing and watching him before it turns back into the trees. His mother believes him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6039"><em>The birth of Conall Dubh</em>, 3 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,540</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6041"></a>**21 an Giblean, FE 1,565** — *The watch grows to nine* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). Conall Dubh's sister and two cousins join his watch at the wood's edge, and within five years of his own first sighting nine keep it by turns, waiting on a beast none of them can explain to a stranger's satisfaction.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6040"><em>Conall Dubh sees the black horned beast</em>, 23 am Màrt, FE 1,560</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0114"></a>**15 an t-Samhain, FE 1,569** — *The watchers of the dark wood* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). A small company settles at the edge of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, the wood never cleared, and keeps watch for a black horned beast that they say walks in it. The people of Cathair dhearg call them the wood-watchers. None of their own accounts is older than Òrd Mhacha, the order of Macha, which afterwards claims them and takes the beast for a sign of Dubh Sainglenn, the black horse.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-6039"><em>The birth of Conall Dubh</em>, 3 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,540</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-6040"><em>Conall Dubh sees the black horned beast</em>, 23 am Màrt, FE 1,560</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-6041"><em>The watch grows to nine</em>, 21 an Giblean, FE 1,565</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6042"></a>**4 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,569** — *The wood called sacred* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). The watchers, near thirty now and housed in a turf hut at the wood's edge, are named the wood-watchers by the people of Cathair dhearg, and a Hall clerk counting the season's coal is the first outsider to write Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag sacred in his own report.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0114"><em>The watchers of the dark wood</em>, 15 an t-Samhain, FE 1,569</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6041"><em>The watch grows to nine</em>, 21 an Giblean, FE 1,565</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0115"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,576** — *The wood-watchers in the stag's grove* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). Wood-watchers come east and cut a black-barked tree in Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, saying that the beast had shown it to them. The stag's people call it theft from a place of teaching. Both sides send to Dùn dhearg and to Dùn ìseal.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6043"></a>**22 an Gearran, FE 1,578** — *The death of a teaching elder* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). In the second winter of the two orders' silence over the cut tree, the teacher who first spoke for the stag's people dies of an ordinary winter cough. Conall Dubh crosses to the teaching-circle unbidden to say he is sorry for their loss, the first word either side has spoken to the other.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6042"><em>The wood called sacred</em>, 4 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,569</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0116"></a>**12 am Faoilleach, FE 1,581** — *The stag's people claim the dark wood* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). In answer the stag's people send teachers west to hold their lessons in Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, saying that the first stag came from there. Now each side claims both woods, and in either wood the two companies meet and do not speak.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-6043"><em>The death of a teaching elder</em>, 22 an Gearran, FE 1,578</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0117"></a>**10 an Gearran, FE 1,589** — *The holy-wood dispute*. Rival rites contend for Coille Naomh Muileann chiar and Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, the first such strife that is remembered. It is settled by dividing the keeping of the woods, and no side is judged the victor.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6044"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, FE 1,593** — *Fearchar Òg brought to the hall* (Dùn ìseal). A boy of seven, a great-grandson of the house that once held Dùn dhearg, is brought to Dùn ìseal by his mother's hand and acknowledged heir by the Keeper of that year, the first claim in longer than the roll can say with certainty found worth the Hall's confidence.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6045"></a>**18 an Gearran, FE 1,595** — *Calum Liath takes the flame* (Dùn ìseal). Calum Liath is made Keeper at forty-five, in Fearchar Òg's ninth year, and judges at once that the wood-watchers and the stag's people will share their silence forever unless someone outside both orders sets a boundary between them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6044"><em>Fearchar Òg brought to the hall</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, FE 1,593</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0118"></a>**11 am Màrt, FE 1,595** — *The boundary stones of the woods* (Dùn dhearg). The woods are divided at Dùn dhearg before Fearchar Òg, a rìgh of Ealasaid Chiar's line who had come to the hall as a boy, and the Keeper Calum Liath. The stag's people keep the eastern wood and the wood-watchers the western, and each may walk in the other's wood unarmed and without cutting. Boundary stones are set at the edges of both woods with the terms cut on them in stag-letters. Two of the eastern stones remain.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-6044"><em>Fearchar Òg brought to the hall</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, FE 1,593</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-6045"><em>Calum Liath takes the flame</em>, 18 an Gearran, FE 1,595</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6046"></a>**8 an Giblean, FE 1,595** — *Conall Dubh walks the eastern wood* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). The day after the last boundary stone is set, Conall Dubh walks unarmed into Coille Naomh Muileann chiar for the first time in his life, a guest under the terms he helped make, and stands a while at the border stand before turning home.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0118"><em>The boundary stones of the woods</em>, 11 am Màrt, FE 1,595</a>.</span>

## The Years FE 1,601 – 1,800

- <a id="ev-EIII-6047"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, FE 1,601** — *The households of the northern road go short* (Baile Mòr mhòr). With cutters set to counting rather than cutting, the waypoint-keepers send less than the Law's full measure to households a day's carry and more from the mountain, marking each short delivery against a day it might be made good.
- <a id="ev-II-0119"></a>**9 an Giblean, FE 1,602** — *Calum Liath's surveyors* (Dùn ìseal). The Keeper Calum Liath sends cutters with knotted cords and lamps into every gallery at Dùn ìseal, to follow the vein as far as it can be followed and mark where it thickens and thins. The work keeps the cutters from the coal for three seasons, and the households go short to pay for it.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6048"></a>**23 an Giblean, FE 1,602** — *Calum Liath sends cutters to measure the vein* (Dùn ìseal). The Keeper Calum Liath gives every cutter of Dùn ìseal a knotted cord and a lamp of the Hall's own oil, and sends them into the galleries to walk the vein from end to end and mark on slates where it runs thick and where it runs to blind rock.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0119"><em>Calum Liath's surveyors</em>, 9 an Giblean, FE 1,602</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6047"><em>The households of the northern road go short</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, FE 1,601</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6049"></a>**27 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,602** — *A steward of the northern road questions the Keeper* (Dùn ìseal). Three households short of their measure send the steward Uisdean to Dùn ìseal to ask whether the counting will end before their own stores do. Calum Liath answers only that he cannot yet say, and the steward walks home with the truth and nothing else.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6048"><em>Calum Liath sends cutters to measure the vein</em>, 23 an Giblean, FE 1,602</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6050"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,602** — *Two cutters lost a day in an old working* (Dùn ìseal). Sent to measure a gallery cut and abandoned in Fionnlagh Dall's time, two young cutters lose a full day in the dark and come out half starved, saying only that they heard something moving beyond their lamp's reach.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6049"><em>A steward of the northern road questions the Keeper</em>, 27 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,602</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0120"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, FE 1,607** — *The measuring of the vein*. For the first time men try to reckon how much coal the mountain holds. Their reckoning proves far too hopeful.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6051"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,607** — *The clerk Mòr nic Aonghais cuts the reckoning* (Dùn ìseal). A clerk of the Hall who learned her letters from a wanderer of the stag's school sets the sum of the cords into a slab of grey stone, reckoning the mountain's coal against the grains in the granaries of Dùn dhearg, the largest measure a household could hold in its own hand and believe.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0120"><em>The measuring of the vein</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, FE 1,607</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6050"><em>Two cutters lost a day in an old working</em>, 5 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,602</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0121"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,607** — *The reckoning of the cords* (Dùn ìseal). The reckoning of Calum Liath is cut on a slab in the Hall at Dùn ìseal: the mountain can give every household its handful for more generations than there are grains in the granaries of Dùn dhearg. It is read out at the council and heard in silence, and the Hall takes the silence for assent.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-6051"><em>The clerk Mòr nic Aonghais cuts the reckoning</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,607</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6052"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,607** — *The reckoning read and met with silence* (Dùn ìseal). Calum Liath reads the slab's sum to the assembled stewards and hearths at Dùn ìseal. No one speaks against it and no one praises it; the northern stewards, who paid for the counting in short seasons, say nothing at all, and the Hall takes the silence for assent.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0121"><em>The reckoning of the cords</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,607</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6051"><em>The clerk Mòr nic Aonghais cuts the reckoning</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,607</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6053"></a>**6 an Giblean, FE 1,620** — *Ealasaid Rìoghach asks the council what is owed* (Dùn ìseal). Griogair's mother stands before the council at Dùn ìseal and asks what the Hall owes her son, sent into a gallery already marked dangerous by a slate no cutter had carried down in memory. The council has no answer ready.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6052"><em>The reckoning read and met with silence</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,607</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0122"></a>**22 an Gearran, FE 1,621** — *The deaths in the lower gallery* (Dùn ìseal). Two youths of the nine hearths, sent into the lower gallery at Dùn ìseal without a Keeper's cutter to guide them, break the wrong face and are crushed. They had been less than a season in the galleries. Their families ask the council what the Hall owes them, and the council has no answer.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-6053"><em>Ealasaid Rìoghach asks the council what is owed</em>, 6 an Giblean, FE 1,620</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6054"></a>**19 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,621** — *Griogair mac Dhonnchaidh and Sìne Bheag crushed in the lower gallery* (Dùn ìseal). Sent without a Keeper's cutter to bring up a left basket, two youths of one season in the galleries break a face already marked unsound on Aonghas's own slates two years before. Griogair dies at once; Sìne Bheag does not outlive the digging.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0122"><em>The deaths in the lower gallery</em>, 22 an Gearran, FE 1,621</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6053"><em>Ealasaid Rìoghach asks the council what is owed</em>, 6 an Giblean, FE 1,620</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6055"></a>**8 an t-Sultain, FE 1,621** — *The council sits three days and turns from fault to custom* (Dùn ìseal). The stewards of the great shares spend a first day laying blame before Ealasaid Rìoghach's second asking turns the council from fault to remedy: a binding of seven years before any young Dia-thìrich may touch the vein alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6054"><em>Griogair mac Dhonnchaidh and Sìne Bheag crushed in the lower gallery</em>, 19 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,621</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6056"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, FE 1,621** — *The apprentice-binding custom is agreed* (Dùn ìseal). The council of Dùn ìseal sets down that no young Dia-thìrich will go into any gallery of the vein's custody until bound seven years to a master cutter of proven years, to learn the mountain's marks and unsound faces before working it alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6055"><em>The council sits three days and turns from fault to custom</em>, 8 an t-Sultain, FE 1,621</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0123"></a>**24 am Faoilleach, FE 1,628** — *The apprentice-binding custom*. Young Dia-thìrich are first bound for seven years to a master of the vein's custody before they may go near the coal themselves. Every later guild of the mines is shaped on this binding.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-6055"><em>The council sits three days and turns from fault to custom</em>, 8 an t-Sultain, FE 1,621</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-6056"><em>The apprentice-binding custom is agreed</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, FE 1,621</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6057"></a>**21 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,628** — *Calum Liath dies at the Hall's door* (Dùn ìseal). The Keeper Calum Liath dies by the doorway where he had the reckoning-slab set, in the ninth year after it was cut, and is carried up to lie among the Keepers' own dead near the two youths he had buried before him.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6058"></a>**29 an Lùnastal, FE 1,628** — *Oighrig Bhàn chosen Keeper* (Dùn ìseal). The nine hearths choose Oighrig Bhàn, a woman of the northern road who had sat with Calum Liath through his last winter, to hold the flame after him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6057"><em>Calum Liath dies at the Hall's door</em>, 21 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6059"></a>**7 an t-Sultain, FE 1,628** — *Oighrig Bhàn asks why the binding stands unkept* (Dùn ìseal). Within her first year Oighrig Bhàn asks why the apprentice-binding, agreed by the council after Griogair and Sìne Bheag's deaths, still stands only as a thing sworn and not a thing done, and finds no better answer than that grief cools faster than custom is kept.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0123"><em>The apprentice-binding custom</em>, 24 am Faoilleach, FE 1,628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0124"></a>**21 an Giblean, FE 1,634** — *Oighrig Bhàn's first bound* (Dùn ìseal). Oighrig Bhàn, Keeper after Calum Liath, binds the first twelve apprentices under the new custom at Dùn ìseal, each to a master cutter by name. They swear on the stone cup to serve seven years before they touch the vein. Four of the twelve are afterwards Keepers, which is the best that can be said for the custom.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6060"></a>**22 an Cèitean, FE 1,634** — *Oighrig Bhàn binds the first twelve apprentices* (Dùn ìseal). In the Hall's own doorway Oighrig Bhàn binds twelve apprentices by name to twelve master cutters, each swearing on the stone cup to serve seven years before touching the vein alone. She stands through every oath and does not sit until the last is sworn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0124"><em>Oighrig Bhàn's first bound</em>, 21 an Giblean, FE 1,634</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6059"><em>Oighrig Bhàn asks why the binding stands unkept</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, FE 1,628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6061"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, FE 1,634** — *Four of the twelve later hold the flame* (Dùn ìseal). Of the twelve first bound under Oighrig Bhàn, four in later years are themselves chosen Keeper, which the reciters of Dùn ìseal count the custom's best proof, though none of it answers in full the question Ealasaid Rìoghach asked.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6060"><em>Oighrig Bhàn binds the first twelve apprentices</em>, 22 an Cèitean, FE 1,634</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-6062"></a>**6 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,640** — *Rìoghnach writes the first strike-book entry* (Cnoc bhàn). A novice of the first bound company at Cnoc bhàn, Rìoghnach, sets down the school's first written account by lamp-light in a hand still stiff from her letters: three words, I struck a stroke, and the day beneath them.
- <a id="ev-EIII-6063"></a>**5 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,640** — *The birth of Mòrag Dhubh* (Cnoc mhòr). Aonghas Ruadh and Sìne of Cnoc mhòr have a daughter, black-haired against the fairness of both their houses, and name her Mòrag. She is raised at a hearth already full of staves and toll-talk, in the first winters of the hall's new silver.
- <a id="ev-II-0125"></a>**23 am Màrt, FE 1,641** — *The stag's people take apprentices* (Cnoc bhàn). The house of the stag's people at Cnoc bhàn takes the seven years for its own cutters and adds a rule: an apprentice keeps a written account of every stroke, and the account is read. These strike-books are the school's chief record for the rest of the age.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-6062"><em>Rìoghnach writes the first strike-book entry</em>, 6 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,640</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7001"></a>**17 an Giblean, FE 1,641** — *Cnoc bhàn takes up the seven-year binding* (Cnoc bhàn). Hearing of the binding at Dùn ìseal, the stag's teachers of Cnoc bhàn take up the seven years for their own cutters, binding each apprentice to a master of the school as the Hall bound its own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0125"><em>The stag's people take apprentices</em>, 23 am Màrt, FE 1,641</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6062"><em>Rìoghnach writes the first strike-book entry</em>, 6 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,640</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7002"></a>**9 an Dàmhair, FE 1,641** — *Cnoc bhàn adds the written account of every stroke* (Cnoc bhàn). The teachers of Cnoc bhàn set a rule the Hall never made: that every bound apprentice keep, once the stag-letters are learned, a written account of every stroke cut in a season, so a master may read back exactly where the hand went wrong.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0125"><em>The stag's people take apprentices</em>, 23 am Màrt, FE 1,641</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7001"><em>Cnoc bhàn takes up the seven-year binding</em>, 17 an Giblean, FE 1,641</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7003"></a>**25 an Cèitean, FE 1,642** — *Aonghas Ruadh is paid in the first silver rings* (Ceann leathan). Among the guards of the southern ford paid that winter in Fearchar Òg's new stamped rings is Aonghas Ruadh of Cnoc mhòr, who carries his home turning it over in his hand, unsure at first that so small a weight can be a whole season's wage. His wife Sìne trades it for cloth within the week and proves him wrong.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-6063"><em>The birth of Mòrag Dhubh</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,640</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0126"></a>**18 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,647** — *The long reign of Fearchar Òg* (Dùn dhearg). Fearchar Òg, who divided the woods, rules long at Dùn dhearg and is remembered chiefly for dying old. He was named Òg, the young, for coming to the hall as a boy, and the name stuck.
- <a id="ev-EIII-7004"></a>**3 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,647** — *Dòmhnall Beag sent to keep the toll at Àth ghlas* (Àth ghlas). Fearchar Òg's clerks send a hall-trained man, Dòmhnall Beag, to weigh the new silver toll at the ford of Àth ghlas, where the Griogaraich have kept the crossing's toll by their own standing for longer than anyone can say. It is the first toll-house on any road kept by a man not chosen at the place.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7003"><em>Aonghas Ruadh is paid in the first silver rings</em>, 25 an Cèitean, FE 1,642</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7005"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,648** — *The Griogaraich come round to Dòmhnall Beag's scale* (Àth ghlas). A year into his keeping of the toll-house, Dòmhnall Beag is still unhelped by the ford's own family, until the winter's firewood and the spring floods force first one and then most of the Griogaraich to take his silver for their labour, never all admitting it to one another.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7004"><em>Dòmhnall Beag sent to keep the toll at Àth ghlas</em>, 3 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,647</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0127"></a>**20 an Cèitean, FE 1,654** — *The silver tokens* (Muileann chiar). The clerks of Fearchar Òg begin to pay the road-guards in small silver rings of the Muileann chiar weight, stamped with the hall's mark. It is the first payment in metal by any ruler on Dia-thìr. The rings travel further than the guards do.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7003"><em>Aonghas Ruadh is paid in the first silver rings</em>, 25 an Cèitean, FE 1,642</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7006"></a>**27 an Gearran, FE 1,655** — *Mòrag Dhubh cuts her own staff* (Cnoc mhòr). Having outgrown every staff her father owns, Mòrag Dhubh cuts one of her own from a young ash at the wood's edge, straight-grained and a hand's breadth taller than she is, and carries it everywhere a girl of the southern road may carry a staff without remark.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7005"><em>The Griogaraich come round to Dòmhnall Beag's scale</em>, 2 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,648</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7007"></a>**29 am Faoilleach, FE 1,660** — *Mòrag Dhubh's first bout at Ceann leathan* (Ceann leathan). Against her father's own doubts, Mòrag Dhubh enters the guards' yearly meeting at Ceann leathan, the first woman to do so, and loses in the second round to a guard twice her age and size, who tells her afterward she had the surest staff of anyone he fought that day.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7006"><em>Mòrag Dhubh cuts her own staff</em>, 27 an Gearran, FE 1,655</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0128"></a>**8 an Cèitean, FE 1,661** — *The toll-house at Àth ghlas* (Àth ghlas). A toll-house is built on the ford at Àth ghlas, where the southern road crosses the river toward Ceann leathan, and the road-guards are paid there in the new silver rings. Its keeper is the first sent from the rìgh's hall, and not chosen in the place.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7004"><em>Dòmhnall Beag sent to keep the toll at Àth ghlas</em>, 3 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,647</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7005"><em>The Griogaraich come round to Dòmhnall Beag's scale</em>, 2 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,648</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0129"></a>**9 an Giblean, FE 1,665** — *The road-guards' games at Ceann leathan* (Còmhrag Ceann leathan). The road-guards of the south begin to meet each year at Ceann leathan and fight with blunted staves for a silver ring. The meeting outlives its purpose, and on its field Còmhrag Ceann leathan is afterwards fought. The first winner whose name is kept is a woman, Mòrag Dhubh of Cnoc mhòr.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-6063"><em>The birth of Mòrag Dhubh</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,640</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIII-7006"><em>Mòrag Dhubh cuts her own staff</em>, 27 an Gearran, FE 1,655</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7007"><em>Mòrag Dhubh's first bout at Ceann leathan</em>, 29 am Faoilleach, FE 1,660</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0130"></a>**5 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,665** — *The fair at Muileann òg* (Fèill Muileann òg). Muileann òg, burned in the War of the Roads, is rebuilt as a market town. A fair is held there each harvest at Lùnastal for the trade of the western and southern roads, and from it Fèill Muileann òg descends.
- <a id="ev-II-0131"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, FE 1,665** — *The landing on the Abhainn uaine* (Cidhe Beag). A landing for river-boats is built on the Abhainn uaine at the place since called Cidhe Beag, so that the grain of the lowlands may go upriver by boat and not on carriers' backs. The carriers of the eastern road protest to Fearchar Òg, and lose.
- <a id="ev-EIII-7008"></a>**5 an t-Samhain, FE 1,665** — *Mòrag Dhubh wins the meeting at Ceann leathan* (Ceann leathan). In her fifth year entering, Mòrag Dhubh of Cnoc mhòr beats Ruairidh Fada of Muileann chrom, twice the meeting's winner before her, in the last bout by torchlight, and is given the finest ring struck that season. She is the first winner of the meeting whose name the reciters keep.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0129"><em>The road-guards' games at Ceann leathan</em>, 9 an Giblean, FE 1,665</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7007"><em>Mòrag Dhubh's first bout at Ceann leathan</em>, 29 am Faoilleach, FE 1,660</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7009"></a>**8 an Lùnastal, FE 1,666** — *Ceann leathan's own mark is asked of the hall's smiths* (Ceann leathan). With the guards' meeting grown into a day the whole market profits by, Ceann leathan's traders ask Fearchar Òg's smiths for a ring carrying the ford's own mark beside the hall's hearth-sign, so that the finest ring struck each season may be known at a glance as the meeting's own.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0129"><em>The road-guards' games at Ceann leathan</em>, 9 an Giblean, FE 1,665</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7008"><em>Mòrag Dhubh wins the meeting at Ceann leathan</em>, 5 an t-Samhain, FE 1,665</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7010"></a>**3 an t-Samhain, FE 1,668** — *Muileann òg's households ask a charter for the harvest meeting* (Muileann òg). Seeing what silver a season's traders leave behind them, the households resettled at Muileann òg's ford ask Fearchar Òg's clerks for a charter of the trading already grown up there at Lùnastal, and are granted it, the hall having learned a fed market pays more toll than a starved one.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0130"><em>The fair at Muileann òg</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,665</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7009"><em>Ceann leathan's own mark is asked of the hall's smiths</em>, 8 an Lùnastal, FE 1,666</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7011"></a>**6 an t-Sultain, FE 1,670** — *The landing built at Cidhe Beag* (Cidhe Beag). The hall's clerks raise timbered piers at the old scramble of stones called Cidhe Beag on the Abhainn uaine, judging a river running near empty beside a road worn to ruts a waste the granaries can no longer afford, and put out word for boats to be built to work it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0131"><em>The landing on the Abhainn uaine</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, FE 1,665</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7010"><em>Muileann òg's households ask a charter for the harvest meeting</em>, 3 an t-Samhain, FE 1,668</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7012"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,670** — *Ciorstaidh leads the carriers' protest to Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). Ciorstaidh, who has carried grain on the eastern road sixty years, walks with two other elders the whole distance to Dùn dhearg to tell Fearchar Òg that a river-boat will starve half their households of the wages that have fed them since before the hall was built. He does not turn the landing back.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0131"><em>The landing on the Abhainn uaine</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, FE 1,665</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7011"><em>The landing built at Cidhe Beag</em>, 6 an t-Sultain, FE 1,670</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7013"></a>**5 an Dàmhair, FE 1,672** — *Mòrag Dhubh trades wool at the Lùnastal fair* (Muileann òg). Some years after her win, Mòrag Dhubh walks a season's wool to Muileann òg's fair to trade for cloth her own household cannot weave as fine, and is asked there by an eastern trader whether the tale of the ring she wears is true.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0130"><em>The fair at Muileann òg</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,665</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7012"><em>Ciorstaidh leads the carriers' protest to Dùn dhearg</em>, 2 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,670</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7014"></a>**27 an Gearran, FE 1,673** — *The boatmen of Muileann chrom swear the paddle-oath* (Muileann chrom). The young crews of Muileann chrom who take up the new river trade settle among themselves, without any hall's asking, that no man may call himself one of their fellowship until he has sworn on his own paddle to answer another boatman's need on the water before his own household's.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7013"><em>Mòrag Dhubh trades wool at the Lùnastal fair</em>, 5 an Dàmhair, FE 1,672</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7015"></a>**28 am Màrt, FE 1,675** — *Dòmhnall of Cnoc mhòr swears his paddle* (Muileann chrom). Mòrag Dhubh's younger brother Dòmhnall, who never took to the staff as she did, swears his paddle-oath among the second crews of Muileann chrom the same year her own daughter is born, so that one household comes to hold a ring won on land and an oath sworn on water.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7014"><em>The boatmen of Muileann chrom swear the paddle-oath</em>, 27 an Gearran, FE 1,673</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7016"></a>**29 am Faoilleach, FE 1,680** — *Fearchar Òg dies at Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). Fearchar Òg dies at ninety-four in the hall his clerks first struck the silver rings in, found gone in his own chair by his steward's grandson. He is buried among the house of Ìomhar after a reign of eighty-seven years, the longest the roll can name, remembered chiefly for its length.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-II-0126"><em>The long reign of Fearchar Òg</em>, 18 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,647</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7015"><em>Dòmhnall of Cnoc mhòr swears his paddle</em>, 28 am Màrt, FE 1,675</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7017"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,680** — *Word of the king's death reaches Cnoc mhòr* (Cnoc mhòr). Carried down the southern road by guards paid most of their working lives in Fearchar Òg's silver, word of his death reaches Cnoc mhòr and an aging Mòrag Dhubh, who turns her own worn ring in her fingers at the hearth and says the king made one thing that did not need his hand to keep travelling.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0126"><em>The long reign of Fearchar Òg</em>, 18 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,647</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7016"><em>Fearchar Òg dies at Dùn dhearg</em>, 29 am Faoilleach, FE 1,680</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0132"></a>**11 am Màrt, FE 1,685** — *The river-boats* (Abhainn uaine). Flat river-boats of hide over withy begin to carry grain and salt fish up the Abhainn uaine from the landing at Cidhe Beag. The boatmen form a fellowship of their own, sworn on a paddle, and vie with the carriers for the Hall's baskets.
- <a id="ev-II-0133"></a>**8 an Cèitean, FE 1,685** — *The boatmen of Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). Muileann chrom, up the valley from the landing at Cidhe Beag, becomes the home of the river-boatmen and their fellowship. Its yards build the flat hide boats for every river of the island.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7014"><em>The boatmen of Muileann chrom swear the paddle-oath</em>, 27 an Gearran, FE 1,673</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIII-7015"><em>Dòmhnall of Cnoc mhòr swears his paddle</em>, 28 am Màrt, FE 1,675</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0134"></a>**6 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,685** — *Beathag Mhòr* (Dùn dhearg). Beathag Mhòr, great-granddaughter of Fearchar Òg, takes the hall at Dùn dhearg. The list calls her ban-rìgh, queen, the first so called, and not rìgh with a woman's name after it; the change of word is the list's own.
- <a id="ev-EIII-7018"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,685** — *Beathag Mhòr crowned at Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). Beathag Mhòr, great-granddaughter of Fearchar Òg, is crowned at twenty in the granary hall at Dùn dhearg. An elder of her own line stands unasked and names her too young to hold ground her house has kept unbroken since the ford. Beathag Mhòr answers with silence and a long look, and the crown is set.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0134"><em>Beathag Mhòr</em>, 6 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,685</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7019"></a>**14 an Giblean, FE 1,688** — *Beathag Mhòr rides the northern road* (Baile Mòr fhionn). Returning from the fleece-market at Baile Mòr fhionn, the young queen rides home by the northern road to see a waypoint-keeper's hearth she has never troubled with her custom. She finds the house at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr thin-fed and sends it grain from Dùn dhearg unmarked, telling its keeper nothing of the gift's source.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7018"><em>Beathag Mhòr crowned at Dùn dhearg</em>, 6 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,685</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7020"></a>**13 an Cèitean, FE 1,691** — *Sìleas nan Clach paid before the hall's finishing* (Cathair dhearg). The mason Sìleas nan Clach of Cathair dhomhain raises the red hall at the bridge-foot through two wet winters and a dry summer. Beathag Mhòr pays her in full before the last course is laid, against the custom of paying only on a building's finishing, and Sìleas cuts the hearth-sign into the lintel last of all.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7019"><em>Beathag Mhòr rides the northern road</em>, 14 an Giblean, FE 1,688</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7021"></a>**14 an Giblean, FE 1,692** — *Iseabail nic Fhearchair answers for Cathair dhomhain* (Cathair dhomhain). The harbour-master Iseabail nic Fhearchair comes to the new hall herself rather than send a steward, and tells the queen to her face that Cathair dhomhain has weighed its own fish and buried its own drowned since before the Red Share held a single stone. Beathag Mhòr hears her through and grants the harbour its own charter of tolls.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7020"><em>Sìleas nan Clach paid before the hall's finishing</em>, 13 an Cèitean, FE 1,691</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7022"></a>**22 an t-Samhain, FE 1,695** — *The grain-ship saved off Cathair dhomhain* (Cathair dhomhain). A grain-ship out of the western islands loses its mast off Cathair dhomhain's harbour mouth in a winter storm, and the harbour's own boats reach it first and tow it in ahead of the new town's crews. The rescue is told afterward on both quays, and both towns refit boats against the day the sea might drift the other way.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7021"><em>Iseabail nic Fhearchair answers for Cathair dhomhain</em>, 14 an Giblean, FE 1,692</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0134a"></a>**12 am Faoilleach, FE 1,699** — *The fleece-measure of Baile Mòr fhionn* (Baile Mòr fhionn). The lords of the western plain hold a market at Baile Mòr fhionn and make the fleece of a grown ewe its measure. Grain, wine, cattle and the horses of the plain are all priced in fleeces. The silver rings of Muileann chiar are taken there too, but reckoned in wool.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7019"><em>Beathag Mhòr rides the northern road</em>, 14 an Giblean, FE 1,688</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0135"></a>**10 an Gearran, FE 1,699** — *The hall moves to Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). Beathag Mhòr moves her hall from Dùn dhearg to the town at the western bridge-foot, Cathair dhearg, to sit where the roads, the river and the western harbours meet. Dùn dhearg keeps the old granaries and the graves of the house of Ìomhar. From this reign Cathair dhearg is the seat of rule on Dia-thìr, whatever else changes.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7020"><em>Sìleas nan Clach paid before the hall's finishing</em>, 13 an Cèitean, FE 1,691</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0136"></a>**22 an Gearran, FE 1,699** — *Dùn dhearg after the move* (Dùn dhearg). Dùn dhearg, left behind, keeps its granaries and its pride. Its people go on calling it the rìgh's hill, and for many generations its reeves will send their accounts to Cathair dhearg in no hand but their own.
- <a id="ev-II-0137"></a>**23 am Màrt, FE 1,699** — *The red hall* (Cathair dhearg). Beathag Mhòr's hall at Cathair dhearg is built on the rise above the harbour, of the red stone that names the town. Its foundations lie under the later citadel. The masons cut the hearth-sign in its lintel as though it were a bridge.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7020"><em>Sìleas nan Clach paid before the hall's finishing</em>, 13 an Cèitean, FE 1,691</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0138"></a>**9 an Giblean, FE 1,699** — *Cathair dhomhain against Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhomhain). The harbour of Cathair dhomhain, older and larger, grudges the new seat on its doorstep and refuses the queen's toll on its boats. Beathag Mhòr grants it a charter of its own tolls. The two towns, a few miles apart, are rivals for the rest of the age.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7021"><em>Iseabail nic Fhearchair answers for Cathair dhomhain</em>, 14 an Giblean, FE 1,692</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7022"><em>The grain-ship saved off Cathair dhomhain</em>, 22 an t-Samhain, FE 1,695</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0139"></a>**22 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,699** — *Disputed hands* (Dùn ìseal). The council at Dùn ìseal is asked to judge more quarrels over the right to the handful than over anything else: new households, divided households, households that claim descent from one of the nine hearths without proof. Dùghall mac Raghnaill, Keeper after Oighrig Bhàn, asks the queen for a counting.
- <a id="ev-EIII-7023"></a>**7 an Dàmhair, FE 1,699** — *Dùghall mac Raghnaill takes the flame* (Dùn ìseal). The nine hearths choose Dùghall mac Raghnaill of Sliochd Raghnaill to hold the flame, a man of twenty-nine who left his own house's hall as a boy to learn the vein's reckoning. His first sitting at the cup finds the council floor so crowded with disputed claims to the handful that he cannot cross it unhindered.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0139"><em>Disputed hands</em>, 22 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,699</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7024"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,699** — *Beitris nic Ailein shames the Keeper into asking* (Dùn ìseal). An old widow of the eastern road, Beitris nic Ailein, asks Dùghall mac Raghnaill at the crowded council how he means to judge claims to the handful for the rest of his life without ever knowing which he has judged rightly. He has no answer, and rides to Cathair dhearg within the month to ask the queen for a count.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0139"><em>Disputed hands</em>, 22 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,699</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7023"><em>Dùghall mac Raghnaill takes the flame</em>, 7 an Dàmhair, FE 1,699</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7025"></a>**29 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,700** — *The queen and the Keeper agree the count* (Cathair dhearg). Beathag Mhòr agrees to Dùghall mac Raghnaill's asking before he has finished it, and the two settle on the waypoint houses as the counting's ground, since every household on the island lies within a day of one. The queen pledges to feed the counters at her own cost out of each house's own stores.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7024"><em>Beitris nic Ailein shames the Keeper into asking</em>, 19 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,699</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7026"></a>**27 an Lùnastal, FE 1,700** — *Ruairidh born to the queen* (Cathair dhearg). Beathag Mhòr's son Ruairidh is born at the new hall, grey-headed almost from his cradle. Her household takes the colour for an ill sign; the queen, who has buried enough of her own line's short-lived cousins to know better, takes it for nothing more than a child's colouring.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7025"><em>The queen and the Keeper agree the count</em>, 29 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,700</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7027"></a>**30 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,705** — *Sorcha nic Ruairidh proves a grandmother's claim* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). At the waypoint house An Taigh-seinnse Mòr, the counter Sorcha nic Ruairidh sits six months over one old woman's claim to the handful, hearing it back four generations by name and by story until it stands proved beyond the council's doubt. She writes the four names down in a hand the old woman cannot read.
- <a id="ev-EIII-7028"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,708** — *Ruairidh Cam of Seann Tarr refused* (Seann Tarr). The counters find no coal-right in living memory at the fisher-household of Ruairidh Cam of Seann Tarr, and refuse his claim. Asked whether his house means to appeal, he answers that they burned peat before the Small-Burning Law was thought of and will burn it after, and that peat, besides, is the warmer fire.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7027"><em>Sorcha nic Ruairidh proves a grandmother's claim</em>, 30 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,705</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7029"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,709** — *Sliochd Raghnaill's plea for Seann Tarr* (Dùn ìseal). Dùghall mac Raghnaill's own house takes up the refused fisher-families' cause at the council, arguing that a right so long unclaimed ought to be granted rather than denied. The council rules against it: the Small-Burning Law protects a right already held, not one never claimed. The Keeper speaks neither for the argument nor against it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7028"><em>Ruairidh Cam of Seann Tarr refused</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,708</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7030"></a>**28 an Cèitean, FE 1,712** — *Ruairidh Cam's grandson keeps the light* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). The rebuilt sea-light on the eastern cape is kept by Ruairidh Cam's own grandson, a duty owed to no coal-right but to his family's long knowledge of the cape's rocks in the dark. Asked whether he still holds to his grandfather's saying about peat, he answers that he does, and the saying travels further than the census roll ever did.
- <a id="ev-EIII-7031"></a>**26 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,720** — *The refused roll kept in its own chest* (Cathair dhearg). The roll of the households refused the handful is consulted so often by families proving an old claim through a cousin's cousin that the clerks at Cathair dhearg give it a chest of its own. It is worn soft at the corners within a generation of its writing, more read than the larger roll beside it.
- <a id="ev-II-0140"></a>**11 am Faoilleach, FE 1,735** — *Beathag Mhòr orders the count* (Cathair dhearg). Beathag Mhòr and Dùghall mac Raghnaill agree that every household on the island claiming the handful shall be counted, its right proved or refused, and its name written. The clerks at Cathair dhearg are to write, and the Keepers to judge.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7025"><em>The queen and the Keeper agree the count</em>, 29 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,700</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7026"><em>Ruairidh born to the queen</em>, 27 an Lùnastal, FE 1,700</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0141"></a>**9 an Gearran, FE 1,735** — *The waypoint houses as counting-houses* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). The counters make their stations at the waypoint houses, for every household on the island lies within a day of one. The keepers of the houses feed the counters at the queen's cost, and in the houses the count is afterwards remembered as a good year.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7025"><em>The queen and the Keeper agree the count</em>, 29 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,700</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7027"><em>Sorcha nic Ruairidh proves a grandmother's claim</em>, 30 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,705</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0142"></a>**22 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,735** — *The census of hands*. The households that hold the old right to burn the coal are counted across the whole island for the first time. So it is shown that the burning of the coal was already rationed by rule.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7027"><em>Sorcha nic Ruairidh proves a grandmother's claim</em>, 30 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,705</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0143"></a>**21 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,735** — *The count of hands* (Cathair dhearg). The rolls of the count, kept at Cathair dhearg, give eleven thousand four hundred households holding the right, and some two thousand whose claims were refused. The refused are written on a roll of their own, and from then on it is that roll families search when they would prove an ancestor's standing.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7031"><em>The refused roll kept in its own chest</em>, 26 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,720</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0144"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, FE 1,735** — *The refused of Seann Tarr* (Seann Tarr). Most of the refused households of the north-eastern coast are fisher-families about Seann Tarr who had never burned coal at all, and now find they have no right to begin. Sliochd Raghnaill takes up their cause at the council and loses. The fisher-families burn peat and say it is warmer.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7028"><em>Ruairidh Cam of Seann Tarr refused</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,708</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7029"><em>Sliochd Raghnaill's plea for Seann Tarr</em>, 2 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,709</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0145"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, FE 1,735** — *The light at Baile ìseal* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). The old beacon on the eastern point at Baile ìseal is rebuilt, kept with driftwood and seal fat as the Law requires, to bring the fishing boats of the eastern coast home in the dark. From it comes Taigh-solais Baile ìseal.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7030"><em>Ruairidh Cam's grandson keeps the light</em>, 28 an Cèitean, FE 1,712</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0146"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, FE 1,735** — *The light at Muileann bheag* (Taigh-solais Muileann bheag). The old beacon on the northern headland at Muileann bheag is rebuilt; from it comes Taigh-solais Muileann bheag. Its keepers are fisher-families of the north-west, who pay no toll to Cathair dhearg in return for keeping it.
- <a id="ev-II-0147"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, FE 1,735** — *The light at Àth dhearg* (Taigh-solais Àth dhearg). Sliochd Raghnaill rebuilds the old beacon on the north-eastern cape at Àth dhearg, to mark the way in toward Seann Tarr. From it comes Taigh-solais Àth dhearg.
- <a id="ev-II-0148"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,735** — *Death of Beathag Mhòr* (Dùn dhearg). Beathag Mhòr dies at Cathair dhearg and by her own command is carried back to Dùn dhearg to lie among the house of Ìomhar. No royal journey before it was so long.
- <a id="ev-EIII-7032"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,735** — *The refused roll read at Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). After Beathag Mhòr is carried the length of the island to lie among the house of Ìomhar, the roll of the refused is brought up from Cathair dhearg in its worn chest and read aloud once before the household of Dùn dhearg, so that the hill that gave up its hall might hear what the giving had bought.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0148"><em>Death of Beathag Mhòr</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,735</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7031"><em>The refused roll kept in its own chest</em>, 26 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,720</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0149"></a>**24 an Cèitean, FE 1,736** — *Ruairidh Liath* (Cathair dhearg). Ruairidh Liath, son of Beathag Mhòr, rules from Cathair dhearg. He is grey already when he takes the hall, and his byname is the list's one jest.
- <a id="ev-EIII-7033"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, FE 1,736** — *Ruairidh Liath crowned at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). Ruairidh Liath, grey since his cradle, takes the red hall in his thirty-sixth year, five days after his mother Beathag Mhòr is carried to Dùn dhearg. The crowning is held quietly, in the household's year of mourning, and he keeps her clerks, stewards and reeve in their places.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0149"><em>Ruairidh Liath</em>, 24 an Cèitean, FE 1,736</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7034"></a>**1 an Gearran, FE 1,740** — *The eastern guard doubled* (Cathair dhearg). Ruairidh Liath doubles the guard on the eastern road against toll-cheats grown bold in the census years, when every clerk on the island was walking house to house rather than watching the roads. The guard's pay, more than anything else in his reign, brings him at last to ask something of the silver.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7033"><em>Ruairidh Liath crowned at Cathair dhearg</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, FE 1,736</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0150"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, FE 1,745** — *The Silver Feud begins* (Muileann chiar). Ruairidh Liath demands one ring in five of the silver taken at Muileann chiar, saying the tokens that pay his guards should cost him nothing. Sliochd Fhearchair, the silversmiths' house, answers with Muireach Liath's ruling: silver is not holy, and so not the crown's either. They close the workings sooner than pay.
- <a id="ev-EIII-7035"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, FE 1,745** — *Màiri nic Fhearchair refuses the steward* (Muileann chiar). A steward rides three days from Dùn dhearg to demand one ring in five of Sliochd Fhearchair's silver. Màiri nic Fhearchair, who speaks for the house, answers with Muireach Liath's own ruling that silver is not the mountain's, and sends him home with no other word.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0150"><em>The Silver Feud begins</em>, 19 an Lùnastal, FE 1,745</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7036"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, FE 1,745** — *The guards leave Àth ghlas* (Àth ghlas). Two of the four road-guards at the toll-house of Àth ghlas leave their posts unpaid, the wages standing on a silver toll no one has yet agreed to gather. The keeper Oighrig nic Ailein stands the house through the winter with the two who remain, turning back no traveller and collecting no toll.
- <a id="ev-II-0151"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, FE 1,746** — *The closing of the silver* (Muileann chiar). For three seasons no silver leaves Muileann chiar. The road-guards go unpaid, the fair at Muileann òg trades in grain again, and the tolls of the eastern road go ungathered. It is called the Silver Feud, though no one is killed in it.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7036"><em>The guards leave Àth ghlas</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, FE 1,745</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7037"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, FE 1,746** — *Grain sent unnamed to Àth ghlas* (Àth ghlas). Ruairidh Liath sends grain to the toll-house at Àth ghlas without naming himself the sender, as his mother once sent grain to a hungry waypoint house. Oighrig nic Ailein guesses whose it is and never tells a traveller the story of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0151"><em>The closing of the silver</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, FE 1,746</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7036"><em>The guards leave Àth ghlas</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, FE 1,745</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7038"></a>**15 am Faoilleach, FE 1,748** — *Two apprentices go hungry at Muileann chiar* (Muileann chiar). In the third winter of the shutting, two of Màiri nic Fhearchair's youngest apprentices go thinner than any she has trained in forty years at the fire. She feeds them from her own table and judges that a right is not worth keeping at the cost of the hands that would keep it after her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0151"><em>The closing of the silver</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, FE 1,746</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0152"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, FE 1,749** — *The Keeper's judgment on the silver* (Dùn ìseal). At the asking of both sides the Keeper Dùghall mac Raghnaill rules at Dùn ìseal that the words of Muireach Liath stand, and silver is not the mountain's; but also that the crown keeps the roads the silver travels. Ruairidh Liath takes one ring in ten, Sliochd Fhearchair opens the workings again, and each calls it a victory.
- <a id="ev-EIII-7039"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, FE 1,749** — *Màiri nic Fhearchair's journey to Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). Màiri nic Fhearchair rides to Dùn ìseal in four days' unbroken rain with her grandnephew Tormod and a strongbox of rings struck in Fearchar Òg's reign, to ask the Keeper's judgment on a right her house has never before brought before the Hall.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0152"><em>The Keeper's judgment on the silver</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, FE 1,749</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7038"><em>Two apprentices go hungry at Muileann chiar</em>, 15 am Faoilleach, FE 1,748</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7040"></a>**17 an t-Samhain, FE 1,749** — *The rain-shut hearing at Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). Dùghall mac Raghnaill hears Ruairidh Liath and Màiri nic Fhearchair argue the silver a full day in a hall the rain has shut. He has Màiri say Muireach Liath's sentence twice, then rules each of them right and each mistaken, setting the toll at one ring in ten on the roads, not the ore.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0152"><em>The Keeper's judgment on the silver</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, FE 1,749</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7039"><em>Màiri nic Fhearchair's journey to Dùn ìseal</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, FE 1,749</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0153"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, FE 1,750** — *The Muileann chiar weight made law* (Muileann chiar). In the settlement the silver weights of Muileann chiar are declared the only lawful weights on the roads of the island. Copies in bronze are sent to every waypoint house, and the house of Fearchar is paid for each.
- <a id="ev-EIII-7041"></a>**17 an t-Samhain, FE 1,750** — *Sliochd Fhearchair paid for its own weights* (Cathair dhearg). The crown's clerks pay Màiri nic Fhearchair for every bronze copy cast from Sliochd Fhearchair's own weights, the first silver the house has ever taken from Cathair dhearg rather than given it. She calls it no poor victory to settle for.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0153"><em>The Muileann chiar weight made law</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, FE 1,750</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7040"><em>The rain-shut hearing at Dùn ìseal</em>, 17 an t-Samhain, FE 1,749</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7042"></a>**1 an Gearran, FE 1,751** — *Beitris nic Aonghais casts the first weight* (Muileann dhearg). At Muileann dhearg, Beitris nic Aonghais casts the first bronze copy of the Muileann chiar weight, cracked along its rim from cooling too fast. She keeps the poor casting the rest of her life, showing it to every apprentice before letting them near the good bronze.
- <a id="ev-EIII-7043"></a>**3 am Faoilleach, FE 1,752** — *The hearth-sign struck on every weight* (Muileann dhearg). Beitris nic Aonghais asks leave to cut Sliochd Fhearchair's hearth-sign into the underside of every weight-copy, that a keeper might know the true measure at a glance. Màiri nic Fhearchair grants it gladly, and the two houses trade weights, bells and lamp-bowls for years after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7042"><em>Beitris nic Aonghais casts the first weight</em>, 1 an Gearran, FE 1,751</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7044"></a>**2 am Màrt, FE 1,760** — *Màiri nic Fhearchair dies* (Muileann chiar). Màiri nic Fhearchair dies in her eightieth year, eleven years after the settlement at Dùn ìseal. At her own long-standing word she is buried with the strongbox that carried her rings to the hearing, rather than the ring she wore at her throat.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EIII-7043"><em>The hearth-sign struck on every weight</em>, 3 am Faoilleach, FE 1,752</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7045"></a>**31 am Màrt, FE 1,760** — *Dùghall mac Raghnaill dies* (Dùn ìseal). Dùghall mac Raghnaill dies in his ninetieth year, having held the flame longer than any Keeper before him. The reciters of Dùn ìseal remember him less for the census than for the rain-shut hearing where he told two sides they were each right and each wrong.
- <a id="ev-EIII-7046"></a>**28 an Cèitean, FE 1,780** — *Ruairidh Liath dies* (Cathair dhearg). Ruairidh Liath dies in the red hall at Cathair dhearg in his eightieth year, in the chamber where his mother died before him. His household remembers him as a rìgh who waited where waiting served and moved where nothing else would.
- <a id="ev-II-0154"></a>**25 an Giblean, FE 1,781** — *The bronze-casters of Muileann dhearg* (Muileann dhearg). The bronze copies of the Muileann chiar weights are cast at Muileann dhearg, where a family of casters learned the craft from the silversmiths. They go on to cast bells, pins and lamp-bowls, and their lamp-bowls hold the Law's measure exactly.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7042"><em>Beitris nic Aonghais casts the first weight</em>, 1 an Gearran, FE 1,751</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7043"><em>The hearth-sign struck on every weight</em>, 3 am Faoilleach, FE 1,752</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-II-0155"></a>**24 an Cèitean, FE 1,781** — *Seonag Chrom* (Cathair dhearg). Seonag Chrom, granddaughter of Ruairidh Liath, rules at Cathair dhearg. She gives the clerks a room of their own in the red hall and a wage in silver, and from her reign the king-list is kept year by year and not reign by reign.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7046"><em>Ruairidh Liath dies</em>, 28 an Cèitean, FE 1,780</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7047"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,781** — *Seonag Chrom crowned and the clerks given a room* (Cathair dhearg). Seonag Chrom, granddaughter of Ruairidh Liath, takes the hall at Cathair dhearg in her twenty-first year. Having read the worn, damp-eaten roll of her grandfather's silver settlement, she gives the Hall's clerks their own room and a wage in silver, and the king-list begins to be kept year by year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-II-0155"><em>Seonag Chrom</em>, 24 an Cèitean, FE 1,781</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7048"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,786** — *A teacher of the stag's people comes to Inis bheag* (Inis bheag). A teacher of the stag's people, once a cutter's son, settles at Inis bheag on the northern coast and begins teaching the fisher-marks to children who will never cut coal. The Hall's roll notes the teaching and calls it, in passing, no great matter, since fish have no need of reading.

## The Years FE 1,801 – 2,000

- <a id="ev-II-0156"></a>**22 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,854** — *Inis bheag's school of letters* (Inis bheag). At Inis bheag on the Abhainn bheag in the north a teacher of the stag's people begins to teach letters to fishers' children who will never cut coal. It is the first teaching of letters for their own sake. The Hall's roll notes it, and adds that fish do not need reading.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIII-7048"><em>A teacher of the stag's people comes to Inis bheag</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,786</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIII-7049"></a>**26 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,871** — *The teacher of Inis bheag is buried in his own marks* (Inis bheag).
